rule_citation: Minn. Stat. 216B.164; Minn. Rules ch. 7835 (7835.4013-4015); MN Distributed Interconnection Process (MN DIP) and Technical Interconnection and Interoperability Requirements (TIIR), Docket E999/CI-16-521
applies_to: All utilities (IOU + co-op + muni; compensation mechanics differ by ownership type)
nem_successor: No mandatory statewide successor for rooftop NEM; Xcel Value of Solar (VOS) tariff is optional alternative for Xcel residential/small customers and became mandatory for new Xcel community solar garden (CSG) subscribers under a phased ARR-to-VOS transition effective April 1 2025 (Docket E002/M-21-694)
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap
nem_sizing_rule: <=120% of prior 12-month (or projected) on-site consumption combined with any community solar garden subscription (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.4c; 216B.1641)
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (Average Retail Utility Energy Rate, systems <40 kW AC); avoided-cost/simultaneous purchase-and-sale rate or time-of-day rate for 40kW-1MW; value-of-DER stack (VOS) optional for Xcel, mandatory for new Xcel CSG subscribers
export_credit_value: Average Retail Utility Energy Rate set annually per utility, varies by utility (statewide average roughly $0.12-0.14/kWh); Xcel VOS approx. $0.1909/kWh for CSG subscribers as filed 2025, stepping down for C&I subscribers (~$0.13/kWh 2025, ~$0.12/kWh 2026)
credit_rollover: Monthly netting under 40kW; annual banking option for 40kW-1MW systems
annual_true_up: Excess annual banked credits for public-utility customers cashed out at avoided cost; co-op/muni excess credits canceled with no payment (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.3a and Subd.3(f))
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SA/SB (Minnesota was first state to adopt IEEE 1547-2018 statewide via TIIR, Commission order Jan 22 2020; docket E999/CI-16-521 remains open for Phase II refinements)
ic_application_fee: Simplified process: $100 + $1/kWac; Study process: $1000 + $2/kWac; statewide $30 surcharge added to all applications
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (typically required for larger/study-track systems; often waived for UL1741-SB inverter-based systems under simplified process — confirm per utility)
insurance_required: Not specified in statewide rule; utility-specific in interconnection agreement
ic_timeline_days: ic_timeline_days not specified as single statewide statutory number in sources reviewed; MN DIP sets tiered review deadlines by track (see MN DIP document)
non_export_option: Yes — defined non-export operating mode exists (MN DIP Exhibit B for Energy Storage; Xcel Energy MN Electric Energy Storage Interconnection Guidelines) using control-system settings and bi-directional metering to enforce zero export
storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes (storage nameplate/inverter capacity at point of interconnection generally counts toward system size for NEM/DIP purposes; confirm per utility tariff)
standby_charge: Not specified in statewide statute; co-op/muni may impose DG fixed-cost recovery fee (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.3(a)); public utilities barred from DG-specific fixed fees beyond standard retail fixed charges

rule_citation: Wis. Admin. Code PSC 119 (interconnection); no statewide net metering statute — parallel generation buyback rates set utility-by-utility via individual tariff dockets
applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni (PSC 119 interconnection technical rules apply to all DG facilities <=15 MW seeking interconnection to a utility distribution system; buyback/compensation tariffs are NOT statewide and are set per-utility)
nem_successor: No formal statewide NEM successor; each utility runs its own parallel-generation buyback tariff. PSC reopened a statewide Net Energy Metering investigation (2023-2025) and commissioned a Value of Solar Study (VOSS) literature review with Berkeley Lab/national labs; as of the Sept 2024 open meeting the Commission had taken no policy action and was awaiting the VOSS literature review — docket remains open and outcome could reset buyback rates statewide within the next 1-2 years
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap (varies by utility tariff)
nem_sizing_rule: Not standardized statewide; individual utility tariffs may impose sizing limits tied to historical usage
export_credit_basis: Buy-all-sell-all / avoided-cost buyback rate for excess above NEM threshold, set per-utility tariff (not 1:1 retail beyond the NEM threshold in most IOU territories)
export_credit_value: Varies sharply by utility — e.g. We Energies buyback ~$0.0317/kWh (2026); WPS/WPL retail-rate net metering up to 20 kW; see FILE 2 utility rows for utility-specific figures
credit_rollover: Varies by utility tariff
annual_true_up: Varies by utility tariff
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + IEEE 1547.1-2020 incorporated by reference into PSC 119 (effective per PSC 119 rule revision)
ic_application_fee: Not standardized statewide; varies by utility
ic_study_trigger_kw: Not standardized statewide; varies by utility (larger/complex projects trigger supplemental review under PSC 119)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion
insurance_required: Not specified in statewide rule
ic_timeline_days: Not specified as single statewide statutory number; PSC 119 sets tiered review timelines by DG category
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear (varies by utility; grid-charging treatment is not addressed uniformly in PSC 119 and is a live issue in the NEM/VOSS docket)
non_export_option: Yes — PSC 119 defines a non-exporting Category 1 pathway for co-located storage no larger than 20 kW paired with a non-exporting DG resource no larger than 20 kW, which qualifies for simplified/expedited review
storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes for exporting configurations (storage nameplate counts toward DG facility capacity category under PSC 119); non-exporting storage handled separately under Category 1
standby_charge: Not specified in statewide rule; some utilities (e.g. We Energies) assess a Generation Customer Charge (~$0.059/day) on DG customers — utility-specific

jurisdiction_body: Iowa Utilities Commission (formerly Iowa Utilities Board)
rule_citation: Iowa Code 476.49 (SF 583, enacted 2020); 199 IAC Chapter 45 (interconnection technical standards)
applies_to: IOU only for the codified SF 583 inflow-outflow regime (applies to rate-regulated utilities i.e. MidAmerican and Alliant/Interstate Power and Light); municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives are exempt from IUC rate/NEM jurisdiction and set their own net metering/DG policies
nem_successor: SF 583 (2020) replaced true net metering with an inflow/outflow billing structure for new DG customers starting July 1 2020; MidAmerican tariff effective Nov 24 2020, Alliant/IPL tariff effective Dec 30 2020. Outflow rate initially set equal to the retail (inflow) rate but is scheduled to transition toward a value-of-solar-informed rate once the 5% statewide penetration trigger is reached or by 2027, whichever first — a Value of Solar study/proceeding is the anticipated successor mechanism and is not yet finalized as of last verification
nem_aggregate_cap: 5% of each utility's statewide peak electric demand (statutory trigger for VOS proceeding; current subscription level not confirmed in sources reviewed)
nem_sizing_rule: <=110% of customer's annual electricity usage
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail equivalent under inflow-outflow (outflow credited at same rate as inflow/retail rate, i.e. functionally 1:1 at present)
export_credit_value: Outflow rate = retail rate as of 2020 tariffs (MidAmerican eff. 11/24/2020; Alliant/IPL eff. 12/30/2020); scheduled to move toward value-of-solar basis post-trigger — confirm current cents/kWh in utility tariff
credit_rollover: Monthly billing under inflow-outflow (kWh-for-kWh at time of use within billing period; no long-term banking under strict inflow-outflow design — confirm)
annual_true_up: Monthly per SF 583 inflow-outflow structure; no annual true-up mechanism identified in sources reviewed
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 (incorporated into 199 IAC 45.3, effective per rule dated April 6 2018 edition; rule revision effective 7/16/2025 per Iowa Admin Code updates)
ic_fast_track_kw: NEM/interconnection uses tiered Levels 1-4 application process (Level 1 = smallest/fastest per 199 IAC 45); exact kW threshold for Level 1 not confirmed in sources reviewed
ic_simplified_kw: Not confirmed in sources reviewed for Level 2/3 thresholds
ic_application_fee: Not confirmed in sources reviewed
ic_study_trigger_kw: Not confirmed in sources reviewed (Level 3/4 studies triggered for larger/more complex systems per 199 IAC 45)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion
insurance_required: Not specified in statewide rule
ic_timeline_days: Not confirmed in sources reviewed (tiered by Level under 199 IAC 45)
non_export_option: Unclear — non-export pathway not confirmed in sources reviewed for 199 IAC Chapter 45; recommend direct rule review
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear — not confirmed whether storage nameplate counts toward the 1 MW AC / 110%-of-usage sizing cap
standby_charge: Not specified in statewide rule

rule_citation: MCL 460.1173; PA 341/342 of 2016; PA 235 of 2023; Mich. Admin. Code R 460.901a-1026 (MIXDG rules, eff. 4/25/2023)
applies_to: IOU + AES (member co-ops exempt but many voluntarily participate)
nem_successor: Distributed Generation (DG) program under PA 341/342 replaced net metering for all new customers starting 2016-2019 (utility-specific transition dates); billed via separate inflow/outflow metering rather than net kWh. Legacy NEM customers grandfathered for 10 years from enrollment date, with storage additions permitted without loss of grandfathering per R 460.920(5)(m) if not a 'material modification'.
nem_aggregate_cap: 10% of utility's average in-state peak load over preceding 5 years (raised from 1% by PA 235 of 2023, eff. 2023); allocated not less than 5% for <=20kW projects and not more than 5% for >20-550kW projects
nem_sizing_rule: <=110% of customer's average annual electricity consumption (raised from 100% by PA 235)
export_credit_basis: unbundled generation rate (LMP-based for DTE; utility-specific avoided-cost/power-supply component for others)
export_credit_value: DTE Electric: outflow credited at monthly average real-time LMP at DTE load nodes, power-supply/PSCR component only, not delivery; Consumers Energy and other utility rates vary by tariff rider - see utility file
credit_rollover: monthly netting of inflow/outflow (not indefinite rollover)
annual_true_up: Excess outflow credited monthly at outflow rate; no annual banking of kWh as under retail NEM since inflow and outflow are billed as separate line items each month
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SB (MIXDG rules eff. 4/25/2023; supersedes prior IEEE 1547-2003/UL1741-SA under rescinded net metering rules)
ic_application_fee: $300 pre-application report cap; fast track initial review $100+$1/kWac (certified) or $100+$2/kWac (non-certified); fast track supplemental review cap $1000; non-export track $100+$1-2/kWac; legacy NEM/DG program app fee combined with fast-track fees capped at $50 total (R 460.926)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not explicitly mandated statewide in MIXDG rules; determined by utility interconnection procedures per R 460.920)
insurance_required: Not specified in state rule; utility-specific
ic_timeline_days: Level 1/2/3 use statewide standard agreement; commission order deadlines are 360 days for utility to file procedures, per-application timelines set in utility-approved procedures (R 460.920)
non_export_option: Yes - explicit rule-based non-export/limited-export path via R 460.980: reverse power relay (0.1% export default), under-power relay, small-DER-vs-load exemption (<=50% of min host load), reduced output setting, or NRTL-certified power control system with 2-second trip on inadvertent export >30s
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - not explicitly addressed in DG program rules reviewed; battery kW is not separately capped from PV kW under the 550kW system cap
standby_charge: Not identified in rules reviewed for residential/small C&I; utilities may petition for utility-specific standby/facility charges via general rate case

rule_citation: IC 8-1-40 (SEA 309, 2017); 170 IAC 4-4.3 (Customer-Generator Interconnection Standards)
applies_to: IOU only (municipal and REMC/cooperative utilities largely exempt and set own rules)
nem_successor: SEA 309 (2017, IC 8-1-40) closed 1:1 retail-rate net metering to new customers effective for IOU customers who did not enroll by a utility-specific 2017-2022 cutoff (approx. mid-2022 for most IOUs, per 30-month transition after 2018 enactment cutoff). Successor is the Excess Distributed Generation (EDG) tariff: excess (outflow) energy credited at 125% of the utility's prior-calendar-year average marginal/wholesale price of energy (IC 8-1-40-17), typically ~3-5 cents/kWh vs 14-17 cents/kWh retail. Grandfathering: systems installed/enrolled before 2018 retain full 1:1 net metering until July 1, 2047; systems enrolled between 2018 and the utility's net-metering closure date (the '2022 cohort') retain full net metering until July 1, 2032. After the respective sunset date, grandfathered customers move to the EDG rate.
nem_aggregate_cap: Not specified as a statewide numeric aggregate cap under SEA 309 (unlike MI's 10% cap structure) - EDG is open-ended/uncapped by kW as a matter of state law; utility-specific queue/study limits may apply
nem_sizing_rule: Generator nameplate capacity limited to the lesser of 1 MW or customer's average annual electricity consumption at the premises
export_credit_value: 125% of the utility's average marginal/wholesale energy price for the prior calendar year (IC 8-1-40-17); e.g. AES Indiana 3.9350 cents/kWh effective 7/1/2024, updated annually via March 1 compliance filing - see utility file for other IOUs
credit_rollover: indefinite (EDG credit balance carries forward indefinitely while customer remains on the rider; forfeited to FAC upon account closure)
annual_true_up: No fixed annual true-up date under EDG; credit accumulates indefinitely as a running balance offsetting future bills down to the minimum charge
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (referenced generally; UL 1741 as certification basis - 2018 edition transition referenced in pending 170 IAC 4-4.3 rule revisions not yet confirmed finalized)
ic_application_fee: Not specified as a statewide fixed fee schedule in rule text reviewed - utility-specific
ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Level 1 threshold (>10kW triggers Level 2/3 review)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not a blanket statewide requirement identified in 170 IAC 4-4.3 sections reviewed)
insurance_required: Liability insurance required per 170 IAC 4-4.3-10 for customer-owned generator equipment, maintained continuously while interconnected
ic_timeline_days: Level 1: 10 business days to confirm completeness + 15 business days to approve/deny (statutory deadlines in 170 IAC 4-4.3-6); Level 2/3 timelines longer and utility-procedure-specific
non_export_option: Not addressed as a defined statewide non-export path in 170 IAC 4-4.3 sections reviewed; utility-specific treatment likely required for storage-paired systems - see gaps file
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - EDG eligibility is based on generator nameplate capacity vs. average annual consumption; whether battery kW is included in 'generator nameplate capacity' not confirmed in statute text reviewed
standby_charge: Not identified in rule/statute text reviewed

rule_citation: OAC 4901:1-10-28 (net metering); OAC 4901:1-22 (interconnection services); ORC 4928.01(A)(30)-(31), 4928.67
applies_to: IOU only (municipal and cooperative/REMC utilities exempt from PUCO net metering and interconnection rules; set own policies)
nem_successor: Ohio never adopted a EDG/DG-successor program like MI or IN - net metering remains the statewide framework, but excess generation is credited only at the energy-only ('unbundled generation') component of the utility's Standard Service Offer (SSO) rather than the full bundled retail rate, which includes T&D, capacity, and riders. This produces retail-NEM-like mechanics (single bidirectional meter, monthly netting) but avoided-cost-like economics, since the SSO energy component excludes delivery charges.
nem_aggregate_cap: Not specified as a numeric statewide aggregate cap in OAC 4901:1-10-28 (no MI/IN-style program-wide kW or % cap identified)
nem_sizing_rule: <=120% of customer-generator's average annual electricity requirement (based on prior 3 years of utility-supplied electricity where available)
export_credit_value: Energy-only component of the electric utility's Standard Service Offer (SSO); exact cents/kWh varies by utility and SSO auction cycle - see utility file for current per-utility SSO generation rates
credit_rollover: indefinite (continuously carries forward as a monetary credit on future bills; utility is not required to cash out - credit may be lost if customer stops taking service or doesn't use it)
annual_true_up: No mandatory annual cash-out/true-up identified in rule text - credit carries forward indefinitely rather than being zeroed out annually
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (per OAC 4901:1-22-03 Technical Interconnection and Interoperability Requirements, TIIR) + UL 1741
ic_application_fee: $300 non-refundable pre-application report fee (optional, 14-day turnaround); Level 1 application fee capped at $50 and may be waived
ic_study_trigger_kw: 25 (above Level 1 export capacity threshold of 25kW; Level 2 covers roughly 10kW-2MW per secondary sources, Level 3 detailed study for larger/complex projects)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not identified as a blanket statewide mandate in rule text reviewed for Level 1)
insurance_required: Not identified as a statewide net-metering/interconnection requirement in rule text reviewed
ic_timeline_days: Level 1: EDU must confirm completeness within 14 calendar days, then complete review and notify applicant within 21 calendar days (30 days for hybrid facilities) of complete application; interconnection agreement issued within 10 days of approval. Level 2/3: EDU has 21 calendar days to confirm application completeness; longer study timelines apply.
non_export_option: Hybrid/DER facilities (which include storage) are explicitly recognized in Level 1 review with a longer 30-day (vs 21-day) review timeframe, indicating storage-paired systems are accommodated but not fast-tracked identically to PV-only; a defined relay/control-based non-export interconnection path was not confirmed in the sections of OAC 4901:1-22 reviewed - see gaps file
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - the 120% sizing rule is based on customer electricity requirements, not generator/storage nameplate; whether battery kW counts toward the 120% figure not confirmed in rule text reviewed
standby_charge: Not identified in rule text reviewed

rule_citation: SB 100 (2019), eff. 1/1/2020; KRS 278.465-278.467; PSC Administrative Case No. 2019-00256 (methodology); Interconnection and Net Metering Guidelines (PSC Order, Admin. Case 2008-00169, as updated)
applies_to: IOU only (municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives largely self-regulated/exempt from PSC net metering rate-setting, though many voluntarily follow similar interconnection practices)
nem_successor: SB 100 (2019) ended 1:1 retail-rate net metering for new customers effective 1/1/2020, replacing it with utility-specific PSC-approved compensation rates (each utility files its own 'NMS-2' or 'NM II' tariff based on an avoided-cost methodology - avoided energy, ancillary services, generation capacity, transmission capacity, distribution capacity, carbon/environmental compliance costs, and a jobs-benefit adder). SB 100 also raised the eligible system size cap from 30kW to 45kW. Customers already net metering (or grandfathered legacy tariff, 'NMS-1'/'NM I') as of the utility's transition date retain full 1:1 retail-rate net metering for 25 years from their enrollment date.
nem_aggregate_cap: Not specified as a statewide numeric aggregate cap - SB 100 did not impose a program-wide MW/% cap; compensation rate (not enrollment volume) is the primary constraint
nem_sizing_rule: Not specified as a uniform statewide % in statute reviewed - sizing generally tied to customer's own load (utility-specific)
export_credit_value: Utility-specific PSC-approved 'NMS-2'/'NM II' rate, e.g. LG&E 6.924 cents/kWh and KU 7.366 cents/kWh (eff. for systems in service on/after 9/25/2021); Duke Energy Kentucky NM II 6.2924 cents/kWh residential / 6.3255 cents/kWh non-residential (eff. 1/1/2025) - see utility file for full detail
credit_rollover: Not specified as indefinite/monthly/annual expiry in a single uniform statewide rule - varies by utility-specific NMS-2 tariff
annual_true_up: Not specified uniformly - utility-specific tariff term
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (latest revision) + IEEE 1547.1 + UL 1741, per PSC Interconnection and Net Metering Guidelines
ic_application_fee: Not specified as a statewide fixed fee schedule in guidelines reviewed - utility-specific
ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Level 1 threshold (>30kW)
external_disconnect: Not identified as a blanket statewide requirement in guidelines reviewed - utility discretion
insurance_required: Not identified as a blanket statewide requirement in guidelines reviewed
ic_timeline_days: Not specified as fixed statutory days in sources reviewed - governed by PSC Interconnection and Net Metering Guidelines and utility-specific procedures
non_export_option: Not identified as a defined statewide non-export/limited-export interconnection path in guidelines reviewed - see gaps file
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - not confirmed whether battery kW counts toward the 45kW SB 100 system-size cap
standby_charge: Not identified in guidelines reviewed

rule_citation: 83 Ill. Adm. Code 466 (interconnection); 83 Ill. Adm. Code 465 (net metering); 220 ILCS 5/16-107.5 as amended by CEJA (PA 102-0662)
applies_to: IOU only (municipal utilities and electric cooperatives are exempt from ICC net metering/interconnection rules and set their own -- see CWLP delta row)
nem_successor: Supply-only net metering ("Rider NM"): excess generation credited at the electricity supply/generation rate only, delivery/transmission charges excluded, effective for systems completing interconnection documentation on/after 1/1/2025 per CEJA. Systems fully installed, inspected, and interconnected with all paperwork received by the utility by 5:00pm CPT 12/31/2024 are grandfathered onto full-retail NEM for the life of the system (forfeited permanently if customer later accepts the DG/Smart Inverter Rebate).
nem_aggregate_cap: 5% of the utility's prior-calendar-year peak demand (raised from 1% by CEJA); ComEd territory reported near/at cap in some feeder areas as of 2024-2025 dockets -- check current Illinois Shines/ICC capacity dashboards for live subscription level, not independently confirmed here
nem_sizing_rule: Not independently verified in a hard sizing cap beyond the 2,000 kW (2 MW AC) eligibility ceiling in 220 ILCS 5/16-107.5
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (legacy, grandfathered only); supply-rate-only net billing (new, post-1/1/2025)
export_credit_value: Legacy 1:1 retail rate varies by utility rate class; new net billing credited at ComEd/Ameren electricity supply charge (cents/kWh), which floats with PJM/MISO wholesale costs -- no single statewide value published
credit_rollover: Monthly netting with indefinite rollover of kWh credits under Rider NM; cash-out treatment for retail supplier switches not fully verified
annual_true_up: Annual true-up practice varies by utility tariff (Rider NM); not fully verified from primary source for this pass
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (rule text cites IEEE 1547; ICC dockets and IREC's adoption tracker indicate a transition toward IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741-SB requirements -- exact effective date of mandatory 2018/SA-to-SB cutover not independently confirmed in this pass; flag as mid-transition)
ic_application_fee: $50 (Level 1, lab-certified inverter-based facility <=25kW per EDC Level 1 application form); Level 2-4 fees not independently confirmed
ic_study_trigger_kw: Screens/study thresholds begin above Level 1 (25kW); Level 3/4 full study triggers not independently confirmed with a specific kW number in this pass
external_disconnect: Waived for Level 1 lab-certified inverter-based facilities per standard application form; requirement for larger Levels not independently confirmed
insurance_required: General liability (e.g., homeowner's) insurance required; EDC named as additional insured where possible, per Level 1 standard agreement terms
ic_timeline_days: Not independently confirmed (statutory timeline exists in 83 Ill. Adm. Code 466 but exact day-counts by level not verified this pass)
non_export_option: Yes -- Level 1-4 application forms include explicit Limited Export and Non-Export control fields (reverse power protection, minimum power protection, directional power protection, or export-capacity-value relay control)
storage_counts_toward_cap: Not independently confirmed whether battery kW/kWh counts toward the 2,000 kW system cap or the 5% aggregate cap
standby_charge: Not independently confirmed

rule_citation: RSMo 386.890 (Net Metering and Easy Connection Act); 20 CSR 4240-20.065 (Net Metering); 20 CSR 4240-20.060 (avoided-cost/cogeneration purchase rate)
applies_to: IOU only (rural electric cooperatives and municipal utilities are exempt from MoPSC jurisdiction and net metering mandates; some voluntarily offer similar programs -- see City Utilities of Springfield/Columbia Water and Light/Independence P&L delta rows)
nem_successor: No statutory phase-out identified; program continues under RSMo 386.890 subject to the statewide 5% aggregate cap. Monitor MoPSC dockets -- no active transition docket independently confirmed in this pass.
nem_aggregate_cap: 5% of the electric utility's prior-year single-hour peak load (statewide cap per RSMo 386.890); current subscription level not independently confirmed for Ameren Missouri or Evergy Missouri West in this pass
nem_sizing_rule: No explicit sizing-vs-consumption limit found in rule text beyond the 100 kW capacity ceiling; system intended primarily to offset the customer-generator's own load per definition in 20 CSR 4240-20.065(1)(C)5
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail during the billing period; monthly excess rolls forward at the utility's Commission-approved net metering rate (set equal to the utility's cogeneration/avoided-cost rate per 20 CSR 4240-20.065(6))
export_credit_value: Net metering rate = utility's cogeneration (avoided-cost) rate, refiled biennially (odd years, by Jan 15) with the MoPSC; reported ~$0.03-0.04/kWh range for Ameren Missouri avoided cost vs ~$0.115-0.13/kWh retail -- not independently verified against a current tariff sheet in this pass
credit_rollover: Monthly rollover within a 12-month window
annual_true_up: Any unused credit expires without compensation 12 months after issuance, or upon disconnection/termination of the net metering relationship, per 20 CSR 4240-20.065(5)(D)(6)(d)
ic_standard: IEEE 1547a-2014 + UL 1703-2002 + UL 1741-2010 (as named explicitly in rule text; no confirmed transition to IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB identified in this pass -- flag as potentially outdated relative to national practice)
ic_application_fee: No statewide application fee schedule found; utilities may charge for required metering/distribution upgrades reimbursed by the customer-generator
ic_study_trigger_kw: Not explicitly tiered by kW in the rule; utility inspection/approval required for all systems with distinct timelines by size (see ic_timeline_days)
external_disconnect: Utility may require a manual disconnect switch/breaker/fuse "in immediate proximity to metering equipment" at utility discretion -- not a blanket requirement for all systems
insurance_required: Not required <=10 kW; required >10 kW at $100,000 minimum liability coverage per 20 CSR 4240-20.065(4)
ic_timeline_days: 30 days for systems <=10 kW; 90 days for systems >10 kW (approval/denial notice timelines per rule's standard interconnection application)
non_export_option: Not addressed in 20 CSR 4240-20.065 -- rule predates widespread storage deployment and contains no non-export/limited-export provisions; treat as a gap requiring case-by-case utility tariff review
storage_counts_toward_cap: Not addressed in rule text
standby_charge: Not addressed in rule text

rule_citation: Ark. Code Ann. 23-18-601 et seq. (Arkansas Renewable Energy Development Act, as amended by Act 464 of 2019 and Act 278 of 2023); APSC Net-Metering Rules, Docket 23-021-R
applies_to: IOU + co-op (statutory net metering applies broadly; electric cooperatives calculate avoided cost off Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation wholesale power costs rather than LMP -- see Ozarks Electric Cooperative delta row)
nem_successor: Two-tier structure created by Act 278 of 2023: customers who submitted a Standard Interconnection Agreement before 12/31/2022 (and systems commissioned/interconnected before the 9/30/2024 cutoff referenced in program guidance) are "Legacy"/"Legacy-Transitional" customers grandfathered onto the pre-2023 1:1 rate structure for 20 years, through June 1, 2040 (Rule 2.06.A.1; Ark. Code Ann. 23-18-604(c)(11)(A)). Customers interconnecting after the cutoff take service under the utility's "Non-Legacy Net-Metering" tariff, compensated at Avoided Cost tied to the 12-month trailing average Locational Marginal Price (LMP) in the utility's MISO or SPP load zone (Rule 2.08); cooperatives base Avoided Cost on wholesale power purchased from Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation instead of LMP.
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide/aggregate percentage-of-peak-load cap in the rules; the binding constraint is the per-facility 1,000 kW administrative threshold (facilities above 1,000 kW up to 20 MW require Commission approval under Rule 2.06.B / Ark. Code Ann. 23-18-604(b)(9))
nem_sizing_rule: Facility size limited to the lesser of (a) statutory nameplate generating capacity limit or (b) an estimate of output needed to meet the customer's "highest monthly usage" in the corresponding month (Rule 1.04(D))
export_credit_basis: avoided cost (LMP-based for IOUs; cooperative wholesale-cost-based for co-ops) for Non-Legacy customers; 1:1 retail for grandfathered Legacy customers
export_credit_value: Non-Legacy: avoided cost = 12-month trailing average hourly real-time LMP for the utility's MISO/SPP load zone, updated annually (Rule 2.08); no single statewide cents/kWh value published since it is utility- and zone-specific. Legacy: full retail rate (varies by rate class).
credit_rollover: Not fully specified for Non-Legacy in the rules excerpted; Legacy 1:1 credits function as indefinite rollover through the 2040 grandfathering window
annual_true_up: Not independently confirmed in this pass
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 / UL 1741 referenced only generically ("...standards established by...IEEE...UL..."); no specific 1547-2018/UL1741-SB version cited in the rule text reviewed
ic_fast_track_kw: Not independently confirmed with a specific fast-track kW threshold
ic_simplified_kw: Not independently confirmed with a specific simplified-review kW threshold
ic_application_fee: Not fixed in the rules -- utilities may charge a Commission-approved "standard one-time fee" to recover administrative/interconnection review costs; exact dollar amount is utility-specific tariff language, not stated generically in the rules
external_disconnect: Waived for inverter-based systems if: (1) inverter is designed to shut down/disconnect and cannot be manually overridden, (2) manufacturer-warranted to shut down on loss of utility service, and (3) properly installed/inspected/tested by utility personnel (Rule 3.01.B); otherwise a visible, lockable, accessible manual disconnect switch is required.
insurance_required: No specific liability insurance dollar minimum found in the rules; only general mutual indemnification language (Appendix A Sec. 8)
ic_timeline_days: Standard Interconnection Agreement review: 30 calendar days (Rule 3.01.E). Preliminary Site Review: 30 days (up to 90 days if multiple concurrent reviews). Facilities Study: utility to use "reasonable efforts" to complete within 120 days (Rule 3.04.G).
non_export_option: No defined non-export/limited-export interconnection pathway found in the rules reviewed -- this is a documented gap, not a confirmed absence at the utility-tariff level
storage_counts_toward_cap: Not explicitly addressed in the rules reviewed
standby_charge: Grid charge authorized only for Legacy customers whose facility exceeds 1,000 kW (up to 20 MW) with Commission approval to exceed the statutory limit; initial rate set to $0.00 effective 6/1/2020 (Rule 2.04.A.3.b-c), utility may later petition to revise upward with a cost-of-service showing

rule_citation: Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection and Net Metering Rules (MPSC Docket, as revised); Miss. Code Ann. 77-3-49
applies_to: IOU only (mandate applies to investor-owned utilities incl. Entergy Mississippi and Mississippi Power; TVA-served areas and munis/co-ops largely outside MPSC net metering jurisdiction -- see Coast Electric Power Association delta row noting ~57% of MS ratepayers, co-op/muni customers, are not bound by this rule)
nem_successor: Not a NEM-to-net-billing transition in the ComEd/AR sense -- MS never had 1:1 retail NEM; export has always been credited at avoided cost plus a Commission-approved "Total Benefits of Distributed Generation" (Value of DG) adder. The adder itself was revised by MPSC order effective ~January 2025 / carried into the 2026 Entergy Mississippi Rate Schedule NEM-2: base adder raised to 5.5 cents/kWh (previously 2.5 cents/kWh in the base rule), with a 7.5 cents/kWh rate for low-to-moderate-income-eligible customers (an increase from the original 2 cents/kWh Low-Income Benefits Adder for the first 1,000 qualifying customers, 15-year guarantee).
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of the utility's total system peak demand (kW) recorded during the prior calendar year, on a first-come-first-served basis (Ch. 03 Sec. 102-103); current subscription level vs. cap not independently confirmed for Entergy Mississippi or Mississippi Power in this pass
nem_sizing_rule: No sizing-vs-consumption rule; caps are pure nameplate DC capacity limits (20 kW residential / 2 MW non-residential) plus circuit-level screens (e.g., 15% of Line Section peak load)
export_credit_value: Entergy Mississippi NEM-2 (2026): 5.5 cents/kWh excess-credit rate for standard customers; 7.5 cents/kWh for low-to-moderate-income-adder-eligible customers, per Jan. 2025 MPSC order updating the base rule's 2.5 cents/kWh adder
credit_rollover: Indefinite monthly rollover ("each new Billing Period shall begin with zero kWh credits... customer may carry over any value of energy credit arising from the prior Billing Period(s)"); no annual expiry
annual_true_up: No annual true-up month specified in the base rule; credit balance is cashed out only at account closure/termination, net of amounts owed to the utility (Ch. 03 Sec. 105/108)
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (no specific edition/year cited in rule text -- "as amended and supplemented" language used; IEEE 1547.1 test procedures and IEEE 1547.2 application guide also referenced non-bindingly); UL 1741 similarly referenced without a fixed edition
ic_application_fee: Level 1 (<=20kW, certified inverter-based): no fee unless resubmitted at another level. Level 2 (<=2MW): up to $50 + $1.00/kW, plus engineering costs capped at $100/hr. Level 3 (full study): up to $100 + $2.00/kW, plus actual study/impact costs, engineering capped at $100/hr.
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 3 full-study review triggers above the Level 2 screens (up to 2 MW, aggregate circuit capacity <2MW) -- exact fail-screen kW threshold not independently isolated from the Level structure in this pass
external_disconnect: Required for Level 2/3 (lockable, visible-break isolation device accessible to the utility); explicitly waived for Level 1 ("Level 1 interconnections do not require an external isolation device")
insurance_required: Not required as a precondition for interconnection approval per the rule and standard application form; utilities barred from requiring insurance not specifically authorized by the rule
ic_timeline_days: Level 1: ~35 business days pre-commissioning (10-day completeness + 15-day approval + witness test within 10 business days of commissioning). Level 2: ~35 business days (10+20+5) plus 30 days for customer signature. Level 3: open-ended, study-duration-dependent (10-day completeness + 10-day scoping + sequential Feasibility/System Impact/Facilities studies with 5-business-day agreement issuance after each), plus 30 business days for customer signature.
non_export_option: Not addressed -- the rule contains no mention of "storage" or "battery" anywhere in the text; energy storage interconnection, grid-charging, and non-export/limited-export pathways are undefined gaps in Mississippi's DG rule
storage_counts_toward_cap: Not addressed (rule silent on storage generally)
standby_charge: Prohibited -- Ch. 03 Sec. 111: EU shall not charge any back-up, standby, or Exit Fees to a net-metering customer unless otherwise approved by the Commission
standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable given the standby-charge prohibition

jurisdiction_body: Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) -- applies only to the small non-ERCOT, MISO-served portion of the state (Entergy Texas territory); ERCOT-area distribution utilities/co-ops/munis are NOT subject to these PUCT DG/net-metering rules
rule_citation: 16 TAC 25.211 (Interconnection of On-Site Distributed Generation); 16 TAC 25.212 (Technical Requirements); 16 TAC 25.242 (limited net metering for non-unbundled/integrated IOUs)
applies_to: IOU only -- and critically, only the small slice of Texas still served by a vertically-integrated, non-unbundled IOU (Entergy Texas Inc., which is in MISO, not ERCOT). CRITICAL DISTINCTION: over 75% of Texas load is in ERCOT under retail choice, where PUCT has NOT adopted net-metering rules -- solar/storage export compensation there is entirely a matter of private contract with a competitive Retail Electric Provider ("solar buyback plan"), not a regulatory mandate. Munis and co-ops statewide (in both ERCOT and MISO footprints) are exempt from PUCT jurisdiction entirely.
nem_successor: No statewide net-metering successor -- Texas has never had a statewide 1:1 NEM mandate. In the Entergy Texas/MISO territory, PUCT's limited net-metering rule (16 TAC 25.242) requires integrated IOUs to offer net metering to qualifying facilities, but export is credited at avoided cost, not retail. In ERCOT territory, there is no rule at all -- export compensation exists only via voluntary competitive-market "solar buyback" retail plans.
nem_aggregate_cap: Not a percentage-of-peak-load aggregate cap under 16 TAC 25.242; program availability is bounded only by the per-customer size ceilings (50 kW renewable / 100 kW non-renewable) and standard first-come interconnection processing
nem_sizing_rule: Not independently confirmed in this pass
export_credit_basis: avoided cost (Entergy Texas/MISO territory only via Schedule SQF); not applicable statewide / contract-based in ERCOT
export_credit_value: Entergy Texas Schedule SQF: avoided cost calculated as an average of peak and off-peak rates per the utility's latest annual PUCT filing; no single statewide cents/kWh figure exists given the ERCOT/MISO split and competitive-market pricing in ERCOT
credit_rollover: Not independently confirmed for Entergy Texas Schedule SQF in this pass
annual_true_up: Not independently confirmed in this pass
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 baseline cited in PUCT interconnection application guidance (UL 1741 certification also required for inverters); exact rule-text edition citation and any transition timeline not independently confirmed in this pass
ic_fast_track_kw: Not independently confirmed with a specific fast-track kW threshold in 16 TAC 25.211
ic_application_fee: Not independently confirmed (utility/tariff-specific)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 10000 (16 TAC 25.211 covers IOU interconnections of generators up to 10 MW; screens for review tiers within that ceiling not independently confirmed in this pass)
external_disconnect: Not independently confirmed in this pass
insurance_required: Not independently confirmed in this pass
ic_timeline_days: Not independently confirmed in this pass
non_export_option: Not independently confirmed for Entergy Texas/PUCT rules in this pass; in ERCOT territory any non-export configuration would be a competitive-market/REP contract matter, not a PUCT rule
storage_counts_toward_cap: Not independently confirmed

rule_citation: 52 Pa. Code Ch. 75 (Subchapter B Net Metering, Subchapter C Interconnection); AEPS Act 213 of 2004 as amended by Act 129 of 2008, 73 P.S. Section 1648.2 (customer-generator definition)
applies_to: IOU only (Chapter 75 binds PUC-jurisdictional EDCs; municipal and rural electric cooperatives are exempt and set own rules)
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap identified in Chapter 75 or AEPS Act (unlike NJ/MD/DE)
nem_sizing_rule: <=200% of customer-generator's expected/historical annual electricity consumption (AEPS Act 213 statutory definition of 'customer-generator', 73 P.S. Section 1648.2; raised from 110% to 200% by amendment). Note: PUC's 2016 rulemaking had proposed re-codifying a 200% sizing cap directly into 52 Pa. Code Section 75.13, but IRRC found the Commission lacked authority to add it in regulation and it was struck from the final-form rule -- the 200% limit therefore rests on the statutory customer-generator definition, not the regulation text.
credit_rollover: indefinite monthly rollover
annual_true_up: Annual true-up at EDC's Price-to-Compare (PTC) rate -- default-service generation+transmission supply rate, excludes distribution charges; timing varies by EDC (e.g., West Penn May 31)
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 + UL 1741 (utilities such as PPL now require UL 1741 Supplement B / IEEE 1547-2018 compliance; no single statewide mandatory transition date found in Chapter 75 text itself)
ic_application_fee: Level 1 (<=10kW): $100 flat. Level 2 (>10kW-2MW): $250 + $1/kW + cost of minor modifications. Level 3 (>2MW or non-conforming): $350 + $2/kW + cost of feasibility/system impact/facilities studies.
external_disconnect: Required (accessible external disconnect switch or utility access to one)
insurance_required: Unclear -- not confirmed in sources reviewed
ic_timeline_days: Unclear -- statutory review timelines exist in Ch. 75 Subchapter C but exact day-counts not independently verified this pass
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear -- Chapter 75 does not explicitly address grid-charging of storage independent of net metering; EDC interpretations reportedly differ and have produced PUC disputes
non_export_option: Unclear -- no explicit non-export/limited-export interconnection pathway identified in Chapter 75 text reviewed; likely handled case-by-case under Level 3/facilities study process
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear -- not confirmed whether battery nameplate kW counts toward the 50kW/3MW system cap or only the inverter's AC export rating
standby_charge: Unclear

jurisdiction_body: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities
rule_citation: N.J.S.A. 48:3-87; N.J.A.C. 14:8-4 (Net Metering) and 14:8-5 (Interconnection); Clean Energy Act of 2018 (P.L.2018 c.17)
applies_to: IOU only (municipal electric utilities and rural electric cooperatives -- there are very few in NJ -- generally exempt from BPU jurisdiction)
nem_cap_res_kw: 10 (Level 1 residential; Level 1 nonresidential threshold differs, see nonres cap cell)
nem_aggregate_cap: 5.8% of total annual kWh sold statewide by each electric power supplier in the prior year (N.J.S.A. 48:3-87). This is a discretionary trigger, not an automatic cutoff -- BPU may authorize suppliers to stop offering NEM to new customers once reached, but may also continue past it. BPU held stakeholder workshops in late 2024 ('Jurisdictional Survey of NEM Reforms') on potential reform; docket ongoing as of 2026 -- watch for a live rulemaking that could change this cell.
nem_sizing_rule: No statewide sizing-to-load limit identified beyond the Level 1/2/3 capacity tiers themselves (10kW Level 1 residential / 25kW Level 1 nonresidential / 2000kW Level 2 / Level 3 above that)
credit_rollover: indefinite monthly rollover
annual_true_up: Annual true-up: excess NEG at year-end trued up at supplier avoided-cost/wholesale rate (not retail)
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 + UL 1741 (Level 1 requires UL 1741-listed inverter)
ic_application_fee: Level 1: no fee. Level 2: $50 + $1/kW. Level 3: $100 + $2/kW (per pre-2024 rule; a Chapter 8 'Grid Modernization' rulemaking proposed updates to these fees and thresholds in 2024 -- confirm current fee schedule before quoting).
external_disconnect: Required per N.J.A.C. 14:8-5 general interconnection provisions
insurance_required: Unclear -- not independently confirmed this pass
ic_timeline_days: Unclear -- Level 3 review timelines were subject to 2024 proposed amendments (N.J.A.C. 14:8-5.6); exact day-counts not verified
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-with-conditions -- BPU is actively expanding storage participation (Garden State Energy Storage Program, 1,000 MW transmission-scale target across Tranches 1-2 as of March 2026; SREC-II/CSI Tranche 5 storage adders for net-metered solar >5MW). No blanket prohibition on grid-charging identified, but incentive program eligibility and crediting treatment vary by program track (SuSI/SREC-II vs. GSESP) -- verify per-project before assuming arbitrage revenue stacks with incentives.
non_export_option: Yes -- N.J.A.C. defines 'non-exporting' customer-generator facilities and permits electric devices designed to limit/prevent injection to the grid, used to bypass full net-metering/interconnection study requirements.
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear -- not confirmed whether battery-only nameplate capacity counts toward Level 1/2/3 thresholds or only combined system export rating
standby_charge: Unclear

rule_citation: 26 Del. C. Section 1014 (Net Energy Metering); Delmarva/DEC/DEMEC file own implementing rules per statute
applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni (statute directs PSC, municipal electric companies, AND electric cooperatives to EACH promulgate their own net-metering rules -- Delaware Electric Cooperative and the DEMEC municipal members are NOT bound by PSC-adopted rules and can and do set their own terms; see utility file for DEC/DEMEC deltas)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 2000 (Delmarva) / 500 (DEC or a DEMEC municipal electric company)
nem_aggregate_cap: 8% of the capacity necessary to meet the electric utility's average Delaware transmission peak demand over the preceding 3 years, calculated in MW-AC (26 Del. C. Section 1014, as amended by SB 298 in 2022, which raised the cap from 5% to 8%); utility may elect to stop offering NEM to new customer-generators once exceeded -- current statewide subscription level not found this pass, but cap was raised specifically to buy '2-3 years for net-metering 2.0 discussions' per DEMEC's 2022 board presentation, implying it was approaching the prior 5% cap -- treat as a live/moderate risk area to re-check.
nem_sizing_rule: No statutory sizing-to-load percentage limit found (cap is a flat kW limit per customer/meter class); however customers are only credited up to 100% of their own annual usage -- oversized systems do not earn a payout for the excess (SB 298, 2022), effectively discouraging intentional oversizing even though there's no hard kW-vs-load design cap.
credit_rollover: Annual expiry, CONFIRMED -- SB 298 (2022) amended 26 Del. C. Section 1014 so that at the end of the annualized billing period, excess (net) kWh credits REVERT TO THE UTILITY with no monetary payout and no rollover into the next annual period (this ended the prior practice of annual cash-out at avoided cost). Applies to DEC/DEMEC per DEMEC's 2022 policy briefing; Delmarva DE's practice not independently confirmed but the statutory change should apply utility-wide since it amended the underlying Title 26 statute -- verify Delmarva's specific tariff language.
annual_true_up: Customer selects annualized billing/true-up period (recommended practice per DEMEC is a period ending in March/April, since credits build in summer and are best used through winter; DE Electric Coop initially set Dec year-end amid customer backlash, then moved to a period ending in March). Non-residential customers pay full cost of any new/replacement net meter; residential customers pay up to $200 (SB 298).
ic_standard: National Electrical Code + IEEE + UL standards for systems <=25kW (statutory reference to NEC/IEEE/UL compliance rather than a named interconnection standard doc); IEEE 1547 version/UL 1741 supplement not specified in sources reviewed
ic_application_fee: Not independently confirmed this pass -- Delmarva publishes its own interconnection guidelines
external_disconnect: Not independently confirmed this pass
insurance_required: Not independently confirmed this pass
ic_timeline_days: Not independently confirmed this pass
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear -- no DE-specific grid-charging provision identified in the statute; likely governed by each utility's own interconnection tariff (see Delmarva DE / DEC / DEMEC utility rows)
non_export_option: Unclear -- not confirmed whether DE has a defined non-export interconnection pathway distinct from the standard NEM/interconnection process
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear

rule_citation: COMAR 20.50.10 (Net Metering); COMAR 20.50.09 (Small Generator Interconnection Standards); Md. PUA Section 7-306
applies_to: IOU + co-op (net metering/interconnection duties run to 'electric companies' which under PUA include cooperatives; municipal utilities such as Easton, Berlin, Hagerstown, Thurmont, Williamsport participate voluntarily and are shown reporting net-metering data in PSC reports, so treat as All utilities for MD net metering specifically)
nem_cap_res_kw: No separate residential-only cap identified -- 2 MW applies per customer-generator regardless of class (see nem_cap_nonres_kw)
nem_aggregate_cap: 3,000 MW statewide aggregate cap (PUA Section 7-306(g), doubled from 1,500 MW effective 10/1/2021; ~18.45% of MD peak demand). As of PSC's Nov 2025 report: installed capacity ~1,537 MW = 51.23% of cap, BUT the pending Community Solar pipeline (~2,911 MW: 700 MW awaiting authorization + 1,728 MW in interconnection queues + 483 MW accepted-not-operating) will nearly exhaust the cap on its own -- PSC's central 2025 recommendation is that the General Assembly act in the 2026 session to raise or restructure the cap. THIS IS A LIVE, HIGH-RISK DOCKET for MD deal screening.
nem_sizing_rule: <=200% of the customer-generator's annual baseline kWh use (COMAR 20.50.10)
credit_rollover: Customer may elect (since SB143, eff. 10/1/2023) to accrue net excess generation (NEG) indefinitely rather than annual cash-out; if annual payout is elected, paid within 30 days after the billing cycle closest to end of April at the generation/commodity portion of the rate averaged over the prior 12 months
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (all levels per COMAR 20.50.09)
ic_application_fee: Level 1 (<=20kW): no fee. Level 2 (<=2MW): $50 + $1/kW. Level 3/4 (network circuits / non-exporting / studies required): $100 + $2/kW.
external_disconnect: Not independently confirmed this pass (COMAR 20.50.09 text not fully retrieved)
insurance_required: Not independently confirmed this pass
ic_timeline_days: Not independently confirmed this pass
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-with-conditions -- MD PSC has approved DRIVE Act EDSSS (Electric Distribution System Support Services) pilots at BGE, Pepco, and Potomac Edison (~185.7 MW combined target) compensating customer-sited batteries and bidirectional EVs for grid services, e.g. up to $300/kW-yr for a 10kW bidirectional resource. NOTE: brief's characterization as a 'BYOD storage tariff' program was not confirmed verbatim in sources reviewed -- the mechanism found is the DRIVE Act EDSSS pilot (Order following 7/1/2025 Commission directive), not a program literally named 'Bring Your Own Device.' Underlying substance (customer-owned storage dispatched for utility/grid value, separate from net metering) matches the brief's intent; SMECO was not identified among the filing utilities (BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, Potomac Edison only) -- flagged for verification.
non_export_option: Level 3 (COMAR 20.50.09) explicitly covers interconnection requests to area networks/radial circuits 'when electric power is not exported to the electric distribution system' -- i.e., MD has an explicit non-export interconnection review track.
storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes -- MD's 2 MW cap and 200%-of-baseline sizing rule apply to 'electric generating system' capacity, which for solar+storage projects is generally read to include the paired storage nameplate for purposes of the net-metering system size cap (not independently confirmed against COMAR text for storage-specific treatment -- verify)
standby_charge: Not independently confirmed this pass
