rule_citation: Va. Code § 56-594 (IOU net metering); § 56-594.01 (electric cooperative net metering); 20VAC5-315 (Net Energy Metering regs); 20VAC5-314 (Interconnection of Small Electrical Generators)
applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni, but co-ops operate under separate § 56-594.01 program with their own caps, and municipal utilities (e.g. Danville, Harrisonburg, Manassas) are not subject to SCC jurisdiction and set their own net metering policy by local ordinance/utility commission action
nem_successor: Not closed; Dominion Energy Virginia customers interconnecting after the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order in Case No. PUR-2025-00079 move to a new 'NEM 2.0' tariff that keeps 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting, but changes the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate to $0.05829/kWh (previously avoided cost, ~3.5c/kWh) and adds a $1/month admin fee; all pre-order Dominion NEM customers are grandfathered indefinitely on legacy terms. APCo's parallel NEM case was decided in the utility's favor (no material changes) in Sept. 2025. Dominion required to file revised tariffs within 90 days of the 4/30/2026 order (~by 7/29/2026).
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC (IOU default under § 56-594; co-op default is 20 kW AC per § 56-594.01 program, varies slightly by co-op rider)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 3 MW (statutory cap under § 56-594 for nonresidential eligible customer-generators; individual IOU tariffs may set lower nonresidential program sub-caps, e.g. Dominion caps at 1 MW)
nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of each utility's prior-year peak load (raised from 1% by the 2020 Virginia Clean Economy Act), with 1 percentage point of the 6% reserved for low-income program participants; as of 2026 SCC filings, Dominion and APCo both report participation well under the 6% cap statewide, though specific co-op sub-caps are much closer to full in some territories (see utility file for local subscription levels)
nem_sizing_rule: System generating capacity may not exceed expected annual energy consumption based on the customer's own usage history (no fixed % sizing rule; utility discretion to verify via 12-month billing history)
export_credit_value: 1:1 retail credit throughout the year for both IOUs and co-ops; Dominion year-end net-excess-generation cash-out is $0.05829/kWh effective for NEM 2.0 customers per the April 30, 2026 SCC order (legacy Dominion customers retain avoided-cost cash-out, historically ~3.5c/kWh); APCo year-end excess purchased at avoided cost (~3.5c/kWh, 2019 figure, last published)
credit_rollover: indefinite monthly rollover within the annual period
annual_true_up: Annual true-up date varies by utility (typically customer's April/anniversary billing cycle); excess above what's used in the true-up period is cashed out at avoided cost (APCo, legacy Dominion) or $0.05829/kWh (Dominion NEM 2.0, new interconnections)
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SB (per 20VAC5-314 vendor certification requirement)
ic_fast_track_kw: Not explicitly tiered as 'fast track' in 20VAC5-314; Level 1 process covers inverter-based systems meeting UL 1741-SB certification requirements
ic_simplified_kw: Level 1 threshold effectively covers most residential/small C&I systems (see ic_application_fee tiers); Level 2/3 required for larger or non-certified systems
ic_application_fee: $100 (Level 1 processing fee); $1,000 (Levels 2 and 3 processing fee); $500 nonrefundable fee for a pre-application report; up to $50 inverter-settings inspection fee
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2/3 review triggers for systems not qualifying for Level 1 (generally above small inverter-certified systems; SGF regulation covers systems up to 500 kW)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (readily accessible, lockable, visible disconnect commonly required by utility interconnection agreements; not uniformly mandated in statute for all inverter-based systems)
insurance_required: Yes — liability insurance required, historically $100,000 for systems <=10 kW and $300,000 for systems >10-20 kW (co-op figures; IOU requirements similar order of magnitude, confirm per utility)
ic_timeline_days: Not codified as a fixed statewide day-count in the reviewed sources; utilities target order-of-weeks for Level 1 inverter-certified systems
non_export_option: Yes — non-export/limited-export interconnection paths exist for larger systems seeking to avoid full interconnection studies, per utility TIIR/interconnection procedures (utility-specific; not detailed in state-level source reviewed)
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (not explicitly addressed in state-level sources reviewed; utility practice may vary — see utility file and storage_specific_notes)
standby_charge: Yes — SCC-authorized standby charge for net-metered residential customers of Dominion Energy Virginia above the AC capacity threshold
standby_threshold_kw: 20 kW AC effective July 1, 2026 under HB 1255 (raised from 15 kW AC, which itself succeeded the original 10 kW AC threshold set in 2011 under HB 1983); threshold applies to aggregate nameplate AC capacity of the customer's generating facility as stated on interconnection paperwork, not actual production

rule_citation: W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 (net metering and interconnection standards); 150 CSR 33 (Rules Governing Electric Utility Net Metering Arrangements and Interconnections)
applies_to: All utilities offering net metering (IOU, municipal utilities serving >=30,000 customers, and rural electric cooperatives are all contemplated by statute; the PSC 'shall consider adopting' a rule extending net metering to smaller munis/co-ops, so smaller munis/co-ops may not be obligated to offer it — confirm per utility)
nem_successor: Net billing (fixed volumetric export rate) has replaced 1:1 retail crediting for NEW net metering customers of Appalachian Power Co. and Wheeling Power Co. following the PSC's August 2025 rate case order; new AEP-WV enrollees after an extended grandfathering window (application submitted after 2/28/2026) receive a fixed export credit of approximately 12.4 cents/kWh (67-75% of full retail rate) instead of 1:1. Separately, Monongahela Power and Potomac Edison (FirstEnergy) customers who interconnect on/after 1/1/2025 receive fixed rates of 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), or 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation) per the 2024 PSC-approved settlement (effective 3/27/2024); existing (legacy/grandfathered) customers of all four IOUs remain on 1:1 full retail net metering, with Mon Power/Potomac Edison legacy customers explicitly grandfathered for 25 years from the settlement date.
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC (statewide statutory/PSC-rule cap for residential, per W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 and Level 1 interconnection definition in 150 CSR 33 / AEP TIIR)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 500 kW (commercial cap per current AEP/FirstEnergy tariffs, consistent with § 24-2F-8(f) directive that PSC consider raising commercial cap to 500 kW); 2 MW (industrial cap per current AEP/FirstEnergy tariffs, consistent with § 24-2F-8(f) directive re: industrial cap up to 2 MW)
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of each electric utility's aggregate customer peak demand in West Virginia during the previous year, with no less than 0.5% of that reserved specifically for residential customer-generators (W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8(g)); current subscription level as a % of the cap not published in sources reviewed
nem_sizing_rule: No fixed statewide sizing percentage found in statute or PSC rule reviewed; utility interconnection agreements govern via nameplate AC capacity caps rather than a load-based sizing formula
export_credit_basis: Mixed — 1:1 retail (legacy/grandfathered customers, all four IOUs) or fixed volumetric export rate (new customers post-reform)
export_credit_value: Legacy/grandfathered: 1:1 retail. New AEP-WV (Appalachian Power, Wheeling Power) customers after grandfathering window closes: ~12.4 cents/kWh (PSC order, Aug. 2025). New Mon Power/Potomac Edison customers on/after 1/1/2025: 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation) — rates fixed for 2025-2026 per 2024 settlement, subject to renegotiation in the companies' 2026 ENEC case.
credit_rollover: Indefinite for legacy 1:1 customers (grandfathered 25 years from interconnection/settlement date for Mon Power/Potomac Edison); monthly/annual treatment for new fixed-rate customers not fully detailed in sources reviewed
annual_true_up: Excess credited against the energy portion of the bill only (not fixed/demand charges) for Mon Power/Potomac Edison per 2024 settlement; AEP-WV true-up treatment for new fixed-rate customers not fully detailed in sources reviewed
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (with IEEE 1547.1 testing protocols) + UL 1741-SB (per AEP WV Net Metering Customer Information Guide v2.0, eff. 2/1/2026)
ic_fast_track_kw: Level 1: nameplate capacity <=25 kW, inverter-based, non-islanding, UL-listed/certified per Appendix C of 150 CSR 33, interconnecting at <=69kV
ic_simplified_kw: Level 1 threshold effectively serves as the simplified/fast-track tier (<=25 kW)
ic_application_fee: $30 (Level 1); $50 + $1/kW of capacity (Level 2, i.e. any system not qualifying for Level 1)
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2 interconnection required for any system not meeting Level 1 criteria (effectively >25 kW or non-conforming equipment)
external_disconnect: Required — labeled, lockable, visible load-break disconnect required outside near the utility meter (per AEP WV TIIR)
insurance_required: Yes — minimum $100,000 general liability insurance required while interconnected
ic_timeline_days: Not codified as a fixed statutory day-count in sources reviewed; AEP process includes 10-business-day review windows at multiple steps (test results, submittal review, meter installation)
non_export_option: Unclear — not detailed in state-level statute or PSC rule sources reviewed; utility TIIR documents may define non-export paths for larger systems (see utility file)
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (not addressed in state-level sources reviewed)
standby_charge: No statewide standby charge identified in W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 or 150 CSR 33 as reviewed; utilities have not been found to assess a distinct 'standby charge' analogous to Virginia's — the 2025 AEP-WV net-metering reform instead restructured the ongoing export credit rate itself rather than adding a separate demand-based standby fee

jurisdiction_body: New York State Public Service Commission / Department of Public Service
rule_citation: NYS Standardized Interconnection Requirements (SIR), effective 2026-02-09, filed in compliance with the order in Case 24-E-0621 issued 2026-01-23; PSL 66-j (solar/farm waste/fuel cell/micro-CHP/micro-hydro net metering) and PSL 66-l (wind); VDER Value Stack orders in Case 15-E-0751
applies_to: IOU only - the six PSC-regulated electric corporations (Con Edison, Orange & Rockland, Niagara Mohawk/National Grid, NYSEG, RG&E, Central Hudson). A single statewide SIR governs all six; they do not have separate interconnection procedures, only utility-specific technical requirements documents referenced by the SIR. LIPA/PSEG Long Island (state authority), municipal electric utilities and rural co-ops are NOT PSC-jurisdictional and set their own rules - see the second NY row.
nem_status: Full retail NEM (Phase One NEM) reported still open to mass market, running alongside the VDER Value Stack (net billing / value-of-DER)
nem_successor: VDER Value Stack (Phase One VDER Order, Case 15-E-0751, issued 2017-03-09) is the successor for non-mass-market projects; mass-market residential and small commercial may elect Phase One NEM (volumetric 1:1 netting) with a 20-year term and no annual cash-out per the Order Establishing Net Metering Successor (Case 15-E-0751, issued 2020-07-16). A monthly Customer Benefit Contribution (CBC), $/kW-DC, applies to mass-market and small-commercial BTM generation interconnected on or after 2022-01-01. 2026 utility-published CBC rates, res/small-comm: net-metered PV $0.97-$1.83 per kW-month; Value Stack PV $0.49-$1.28 per kW-month.
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 (PSL 66-j(1)(d) residential solar, kW AC; 100 kW for a farm operation on a residential meter; 25 kW residential wind under PSL 66-l; 25 kW residential micro-hydro; 10 kW micro-CHP and residential fuel cell)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 2000 (PSL 66-j(1)(d) non-residential solar, kW AC; also 2000 kW non-residential fuel cell, micro-hydro and farm waste; 2000 kW non-residential wind under PSL 66-l). The SIR itself covers DG and/or ESS up to 5000 kW AC.
nem_aggregate_cap: PSL 66-j(3)(a) sets a first-come-first-served statutory cap of 1% of the utility's 2005 electric demand; PSL 66-j(3)(b) authorises the PSC to raise it, and the PSC raised it to 3% (2012) and 6% (2014). Reported (secondary) that in 2015 the PSC let the aggregate cap float pending the NEM successor, so it is not a live constraint - not verified against the order text.
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail volumetric netting under Phase One NEM (mass market); value-of-DER stack under VDER Value Stack - monetary crediting of net hourly injections built from LBMP energy value, capacity/ICAP value, environmental E-Value, Demand Reduction Value and Locational System Relief Value
export_credit_value: No single statewide rate. Value Stack credit is $/kWh, varies by utility, NYISO load zone, hour and vintage; Phase One NEM credits at the customer's full retail volumetric rate.
credit_rollover: Monthly rollover of excess credits (PSL 66-j(3)(e)-(h) for remote-crediting configurations); Value Stack credits carry over as monetary bill credits
annual_true_up: Phase One NEM reported to have no annual cash-out (2020 Net Metering Successor Order); PSL 66-j(4)(c) annual payment at utility avoided cost applies to legacy/grandfathered net metering. Annual-cash-out removal is secondary-sourced.
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741 Supplement B. SIR Sec II.H requires NRTL certification to the most recent revision of UL 1741 including Supplement B (UL 1741 SB), with settings specified in each utility's technical requirements document.
ic_fast_track_kw: 300 (SIR Sec I.B Exception 1: inverter-based systems above 50 kW up to 300 kW certified to UL 1741 SB may use the 6-step expedited process at utility approval; utilities are encouraged but not required to use it)
ic_simplified_kw: 50 (SIR Sec I.B: 6-step expedited process for systems 50 kW or less; utility has 10 business days to determine completeness/eligibility/approval)
ic_application_fee: No application fee for systems 50 kW or less (SIR Sec I.B Step 3). Above 50 kW an application fee applies but its dollar amount is set in SIR Appendix F, which was not retrievable - NOT VERIFIED. Other fixed SIR fees: $750 non-refundable Pre-Application Report fee (credited to the application fee if the application is filed within 15 business days); $2,500 Supplemental Screening Analysis fee with actual costs billable up to $5,000; Energy Storage System Protection and Control Review fee = $500 + $4/kW capped at $3,000.
ic_study_trigger_kw: No fixed kW study trigger. Systems above 50 kW up to 5 MW enter the 11-step process: the utility runs a Preliminary Screening Analysis (screens A-F, 15 business days). Passing all screens with no Interconnection Facilities or Distribution Upgrades means no study. Failing a screen lets the applicant choose a results meeting, a Supplemental Screening Analysis (screens G-I) or a full Coordinated Electric System Interconnection Review (CESIR). CESIR is therefore triggered by screen failure or applicant election, not by size alone. Systems 50 kW or less in underground secondary network areas may also require a CESIR (SIR Sec I.C Exception 1).
external_disconnect: Required for systems larger than 25 kW and for non-inverter-based systems 25 kW or less - external, manual, visible, gang-operated, load-break, lockable in the open position, customer-owned (SIR Sec II.D). Waived for inverter-based systems 25 kW or less.
insurance_required: No statewide requirement. PSL 66-j(5)(b)(i) and 66-j(5-a)(c) bar an electric corporation from requiring additional liability insurance from a net-metered customer-generator whose equipment meets the established safety standards. The SIR imposes no insurance requirement.
ic_timeline_days: Per-step business-day deadlines, not one statutory clock: 10 BD application completeness/eligibility/approval determination; 15 BD Preliminary Screening Analysis; 20 BD Supplemental Screening Analysis; 20 BD ESS Protection and Control Review; 10 BD verification testing after notice; 5 BD final acceptance letter. CESIR duration is project-specific and not fixed by the SIR.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes - the SIR expressly studies an ESS's Maximum Import as well as Maximum Export (Sec I.E Step 2 and Glossary), so grid charging is a declared, permitted operating characteristic. On the compensation side, the Joint Utilities' Value Stack Hybrid Facilities tariff Options C and D allow the storage to be charged from both the paired generator and the utility system and allow both to inject for compensation, while Options A and B restrict charging to the paired generator so that injections keep E-Value, ICAP and Market Transition Credit eligibility. The precise crediting of grid-charged kWh under Options C/D was not verified against tariff text, and the Joint Utilities have petitioned to apply standby and buyback service to Option C/D hybrids whose NEM-eligible generator is smaller than the paired ESS (Case 15-E-0751) - disposition of that petition not verified.
non_export_option: Yes - Appendix K requires the applicant to declare the ESS's Maximum Export (which may be set to zero or a limited value) and the utility studies the facility at those declared operating characteristics; for ESS requiring a CESIR the utility supplies testing procedures that use the applicant's load management control systems to limit reverse power (SIR Sec I.E Step 2). Systems neither designed to operate nor operating in parallel with the utility system are outside the SIR entirely (SIR Sec I.A). A change of operating characteristics later requires a new Appendix K and a contract amendment.
storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes for SIR tier routing - which process applies (Sec I.B vs I.C) is set by the sum of the AC nameplate ratings of all DG and ESS behind the point of common coupling, and maximum export is capped at 5 MW AC (SIR Sec I.A and I.E Step 1). Whether ESS kW counts against the PSL 66-j net metering system-size caps is not addressed in the SIR - Unclear.
standby_charge: Authorized, with a net-metering carve-out. PSL 66-j(4)(d) bars an electric corporation from imposing back-up, standby or demand charges on a net-metered customer-generator, except that ordinary demand charges may be applied on the same terms as to non-generating customers in the same class. Utility standby-service and buyback tariffs apply outside net metering (e.g. Con Edison General Rule 20 standby service, Rider Q standby pilot rate, SC-11 buyback).
standby_threshold_kw: Set by each utility's tariff, not statewide.

jurisdiction_body: Long Island Power Authority (Board of Trustees); PSEG Long Island administers as LIPA's agent
rule_citation: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service, Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (SGIP) addendum; separate LIPA Smart Grid Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (SGSGIP) track
applies_to: LIPA / PSEG Long Island only. LIPA is a state authority and is NOT subject to the PSC's Standardized Interconnection Requirements, PSL 66-j or PSL 66-l; it runs its own SGIP.
nem_status: Full retail NEM (Phase One Net Billing, 1:1 monthly volumetric crediting) for Mass Market residential/small-commercial customers and pre-2018/2020 Large Onsite projects, running alongside a Value Stack (VDER-analogue) tariff for Large Onsite/Offsite projects and Community Distributed Generation (CDG). Verified against LIPA Tariff for Electric Service Leaf Nos. 34A-34K (Sec I.C.15, Net Metering Generators) and LIPA Statement No. 102 (Value Stack Credits/VSC), effective 2026-09-01.
nem_successor: Value Stack (VSC) tariff, a VDER-style compensation construct - confirmed in LIPA Tariff Leaf 34C Sec I.C.15.c)(5)-(6) and priced in LIPA Statement No. 102 (VSC), effective 2026-09-01. Applies to Large Onsite/Offsite projects and CDG; Mass Market/Phase One NEM customers are not forced onto it and may keep 1:1 net billing (and may pair on-site storage without losing NEM eligibility).
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC for Residential Solar, Wind, Micro-Hydroelectric, or hybrid combinations; Residential Farm 100 kW (Solar) or 500 kW (Wind) or 500 kW (hybrid); Farm Waste 5,000 kW; Micro-CHP 1-10 kW; Fuel Cell <=10 kW. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34A/34A-1, Sec I.C.15.a)] - LIPA voluntarily mirrors the PSL 66-j/66-l residential thresholds even though it states it is not subject to PSL 66-j.
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 5,000 kW AC for Nonresidential Solar, Wind, Farm Waste, Fuel Cell or Micro-Hydroelectric. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34B, Sec I.C.15.b)(1)] - notably larger than the PSC utilities' 2,000 kW PSL 66-j cap; existing 2,000-5,000 kW generators not yet on Value Stack may opt in to VDER (Leaf 34B, (2)).
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide-style aggregate/program MW or % cap found in the LIPA Tariff's General Terms and Conditions, unlike the PSC utilities' former 1%->6%-of-2005-peak-load cap under PSL 66-j. Consistent with LIPA's own confirmation that it is 'not subject to PSL Section 66-j' (LIPA Dec-2025 Tariff Changes filing, Exhibit B-3 background section, citing Case 19-E-0079). Current subscription level, if tracked, was not found in this pass.
nem_sizing_rule: Residential (Solar/Wind/Micro-Hydro/hybrid): system capacity <=110% of the customer's prior 12-month consumption or a customer-provided load letter, and within the kW caps above. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34A, Sec I.C.15.a)(1)] Nonresidential: no consumption-matching sizing rule found beyond the 5,000 kW capacity cap [Leaf 34B].
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail volumetric netting for Mass Market/Net Billing customers (net excess kWh credited at the same per-kWh rate as non-generating customers in the same rate class, Leaf 34F Sec I.C.15.h)(1)-(2)); value-of-DER stack (Value Stack/VSC) for Large Onsite/Offsite and CDG projects, structurally parallel to the PSC's VDER Value Stack.
export_credit_value: Net Billing: full volumetric retail rate of the customer's own rate class (no separate statewide cents/kWh figure). Value Stack (VSC) components per LIPA Statement No. 102, effective 2026-09-01: Energy Component = NYISO day-ahead zonal LBMP average; Capacity Component Alt.1 (Sept 2026) $0.0339/kWh at 34.3% proxy capacity factor, Alt.2 $0.1797/kWh, Alt.3 $11.0578/kW-month; Environmental Component $0.03103/kWh; Demand Reduction Value $0.4451/kWh (contracted hours); Locational System Relief Value $7.3450/kWh per event; Community Credit $0.0500/kWh (Fuel Cell technology adjustment factor 16%).
credit_rollover: Monthly rollover of banked credits within the service year (banked separately by rating period - peak/off-peak/intermediate - for TOU rate codes; re-mapped when a customer switches rate structure), but not indefinite - see annual_true_up for the yearly cash-out. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34E-34F, Sec I.C.15.h)]
annual_true_up: At the end of the first year of service and on every anniversary thereafter, LIPA pays the Customer-generator for any remaining banked net-excess-generation credit, valued at the avoided energy price per LIPA's Statement of Market Energy Prices. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34F, Sec I.C.15.h)(h)] This is an annual cash-out - a real deviation from the PSC row's Phase One NEM, which is reported (secondary-sourced there) to have no annual cash-out.
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 / UL 1741 Supplement B (UL 1741 SB) - the SGIP requires NRTL certification to 'the most recent revision of UL 1741 including Supplement B' with settings per PSEG Long Island's Technical Requirements and Screening Criteria document. [LIPA/PSEG Long Island SGIP, July 2026 ed., Secs I.B and II.B]
ic_fast_track_kw: 300 - SGIP Sec I.B Exception 1: inverter-based systems above 50 kW up to 300 kW, UL 1741 SB certified, may use the expedited process at PSEG Long Island's determination. Mirrors the PSC SIR's 300 kW tier.
ic_simplified_kw: 50 - SGIP Sec I.B: Expedited/Fast Track Process applies to systems 50 kW or less. Mirrors the PSC SIR's 50 kW tier.
ic_application_fee: SGIP application fee $750 for systems 50 kW to 5 MW and $750 for systems 5 MW to 10 MW, payable to PSEG Long Island (PSEG Long Island SGIP Application Instructions). Fee for systems under 50 kW not verified.
ic_study_trigger_kw: No fixed kW study trigger. Systems that fail the Preliminary Screening Analysis (Appendix G technical screens) or whose applicant elects further review proceed to a Supplemental Screening Analysis or a full Coordinated Electric System Interconnection Review (CESIR) - structurally parallel to the PSC SIR's process. [SGIP, July 2026 ed., Secs I.B-I.C]
external_disconnect: Unclear beyond an automatic device. SGIP Sec II.B requires an automatic disconnect device (protective-relay based, sized to code, with over/under voltage and frequency trip functions) that isolates the generator on islanding or LIPA-system-fault detection. The SGIP text located does not separately spell out an external, manual, visible, lockable, gang-operated disconnect switch requirement the way the PSC SIR does for systems above 25 kW; LIPA's Red Book electrical specifications (not reviewed in this pass) may impose one - not verified either way.
insurance_required: No blanket insurance mandate found in the SGIP itself. However, LIPA Tariff Leaf 34C, Sec I.C.15.c)(4) reserves the Authority's right to require a Customer-generator to purchase additional liability insurance (along with added safety/performance standards or tests) when total generating capacity on the same local feeder exceeds 20% of that feeder's rated capacity - a real, feeder-loading-triggered insurance exposure that the PSC row does not have (PSL 66-j(5)(b)(i)/(5-a)(c) bars the PSC utilities from requiring it).
ic_timeline_days: Per-step business-day deadlines, not one statutory clock (mirrors the PSC SIR's structure): 10 BD application completeness/eligibility determination; 15 BD Preliminary Screening Analysis; 10 BD applicant election after screening results; 20 BD Supplemental Screening Analysis; 15 BD contract issuance after passing screens; 10 BD verification testing after installation notice; 5 BD final acceptance letter. CESIR duration is project-specific and not fixed by the SGIP. [SGIP, July 2026 ed.]
storage_allowed: Yes - SGIP Sec I.E and Appendix J define a dedicated Energy Storage System (ESS)/Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) application track covering Hybrid Projects (DG + ESS) and stand-alone storage, within the SGIP's 10 MW aggregate nameplate ceiling.
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - LIPA SGIP and tariff not verified on grid charging
non_export_option: Yes, structurally: ESS applicants must declare 'Maximum Export' and 'Maximum Import' as operating characteristics in Appendix J, and PSEG Long Island studies the facility at those declared values (which may be set to zero or a limited value), so a limited/non-export configuration is supported. The SGIP text reviewed does not label this a distinct, separately-branded fast-track 'non-export' pathway the way the PSC SIR's Appendix K is described - Unclear if it confers the same study-skipping benefit.
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear. LIPA's net-metering size limits (Tariff Leaf 34A/34B) are written against the 'rated capacity' of the Solar/Wind/Farm Waste/Fuel Cell/Micro-Hydroelectric generating equipment, i.e., the generator - neither the Tariff nor the SGIP text reviewed states whether a paired ESS's AC kW is added to that figure for cap purposes. The Tariff does confirm (Leaf 34C, Sec I.C.15.c)(5)) that Mass Market NEM customers may pair storage with an eligible generator and remain on Phase One NEM, so storage does not disqualify a system from net metering - but whether it counts toward the kW ceiling itself was not found.
standby_charge: Service Classification No. 12 - Standby Service (renamed from 'Back-Up and Supplemental Service,' new Rate Code 682 commercial / 179 residential-optional), effective 2026-01-01, replacing the old SC-12 Back-Up and Supplemental Service tariff. Mandatory for on-site self-generating customers who maintain a grid connection, subject to technology (solar/wind) and size-based exemptions; optional for other self-generating customers ('Optional Rate Customers,' requires an AMI meter). Rate = Service Charge + Contract Demand Charge, set on an Allocated-Cost-of-Service, revenue-neutral basis; ~72 existing mandatory commercial customers are phased in from 2026-2030 (full rates from 2031) unless they elect full rates immediately. Service Classification No. 11 - Buyback Service (for customers exporting to the grid) was updated in the same filing to add a Customer Charge and Buyback Contract Demand Charge set equal to the corresponding Standby rates; stand-alone ESS that reach Step 3 of the SGIP process before 2030-12-31 are exempt from the Buyback Contract Demand Charge for 15 years from their in-service date. [LIPA Board materials, 'December 2025 Tariff Changes,' Item 3 - New Rates for Standby Service and Updates to Buyback Service, approved effective 2026-01-01]
standby_threshold_kw: No single kW threshold. SC-12 Standby Service is mandatory for on-site generating customers maintaining a grid connection, with exemptions including generation under 5 kVA and generation under 15% of the customer's maximum potential demand; SC-11 Buyback Service is required for customers who inject power to the grid, subject to similar technology/size exemptions. [LIPA Board materials, 'December 2025 Tariff Changes,' background section]

rule_citation: PU Code 2827 and 2827.1; Electric Rule 21 (each IOU keeps its own version; R.17-07-007, successor rulemaking R.25-08-004 opened 2025-08-20); NBT: D.22-12-056 (R.20-08-020) as implemented by Res. E-5301, modified by D.23-11-068 and D.24-09-051; NEM 2.0: D.16-01-044; 20-yr NEM legacy: D.14-03-041; NEM-paired storage: D.14-05-033, D.16-04-020, D.18-02-008, D.19-01-030, D.20-06-017; SGIP-to-NBT transition: D.24-03-071
applies_to: IOU only - PG&E, SCE, SDG&E (large IOUs). The small CPUC-jurisdictional IOUs (Bear Valley, Liberty, PacifiCorp) have separately approved NEM/NBT tariffs and their own Rule 21 versions; PacifiCorp uses its OATT process instead of Rule 21 (D.07-07-027). Publicly-owned utilities (LADWP, SMUD, IID, MID, TID and the municipal utilities) are NOT bound by Rule 21 or the NBT and set their own interconnection and export rules - see the utility file. CCA customers inside IOU territory interconnect under the IOU's Rule 21 and NBT; the CCA sets the generation portion of the export credit. Rule 21 does not cover facilities selling into FERC wholesale markets (those use the IOU WDT or the CAISO tariff).
nem_successor: Net Billing Tariff (NBT), marketed by the IOUs as the 'Solar Billing Plan', adopted by D.22-12-056 (2022-12-15). Applies to interconnection applications submitted on or after 2023-04-15. Exports are credited at hourly Energy Export Credit (EEC) prices derived from the CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator (ACC). Customers must take a specific electrification TOU rate: PG&E E-ELEC, SCE TOU-D-PRIME, SDG&E EV-TOU-5 (non-residential customers may use any TOU rate). The NBT legacy period is 9 years from original PTO, for the original customer only; customers who migrate from NEM get no NBT legacy period. Legacy NEM 1.0/2.0 customers keep NEM for 20 years from original PTO (D.14-03-041 / D.16-01-044); the right transfers with the system at the same location. Switching to NBT voluntarily permanently forfeits the remaining NEM term. NEM 2.0 applications submitted by 2023-04-14 had until 2026-04-14 to finish (Secondary - installer guidance).
nem_cap_res_kw: No kW cap - sized-to-load only (SCE Sched. NBT SC 1.b.iii.B: 'there is no limit on the capacity' other than the sized-to-load rule). 1 MW (AC) is the cost-responsibility boundary: above 1 MW, NBT/NEM facilities pay non-NEM fees, study costs and upgrade costs (Rule 21 D.13.a). Capacity uses the lesser of inverter nameplate and CEC-AC rating (AC).
nem_cap_nonres_kw: No kW cap - sized-to-load only; same 1 MW AC cost-responsibility boundary (Rule 21 D.13.a). NEM facilities interconnecting at transmission level are limited to 1 MW or less (D.22-07-001).
nem_aggregate_cap: None for NEM 2.0 or NBT. NEM 1.0 closed when it reached its statutory program cap (calculation clarified in D.12-05-036), which triggered NEM 2.0.
nem_sizing_rule: NBT: estimated output <=100% of prior 12-month usage (kWh), or up to 150% if the customer attests to expected load growth within 12 months. Net surplus is paid at NSC. NEM 2.0: <= the customer's annual onsite load. Expanding a system by more than the greater of 10% or 1 kW of original generating nameplate triggers the NEM/NBT modification rules.
export_credit_value: Hourly ACC-derived EEC prices: 24 hours x weekday/weekend x month (576 values per vintage year), with separate Generation and Delivery components. Prices are locked for 9 years for PTO dates 2023-04-15 through 2027-12-31; later PTO dates float annually. Residential ACC Plus adder (SCE Sched. NBT Rates 3.b, $/kWh by PTO vintage, non-equity/equity): 2023 0.040/0.093; 2024 0.032/0.074; 2025 0.024/0.056; 2026 0.016/0.037; 2027 0.008/0.019; 2028+ 0. Non-residential gets no adder. SDG&E residential customers get no adder. Customers adding solar required by building code (new construction) get no adder. NEM customers who move to NBT get no adder. Values in cents: 2026-vintage SCE adder = 1.6 c/kWh (3.7 c/kWh equity). PG&E adder table not independently read. Net Surplus Compensation at true-up = DLAP 7am-5pm 12-month rolling average (CPUC: roughly 2-3 c/kWh).
credit_rollover: Monthly EEC credits offset energy charges only (not NBCs, minimum charge, demand or fixed charges) and roll forward within the 12-month Relevant Period. At true-up, unused EEC is forfeited and remaining net surplus kWh is paid at NSC. The ACC Plus adder can offset any charge and carries forward until used.
annual_true_up: At the end of the customer's 12-month Relevant Period (anniversary of PTO, or one-time election to move it). NBT bills are paid monthly; NEM 1.0/2.0 settles charges annually. Net surplus is paid at the NSC rate (D.11-06-016).
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SB (Rule 21 Sec. D.5 and Secs. Hh/P, smart-inverter requirements under Res. E-5000/E-5036). Inverters must be on the CEC grid-support inverter list. Earlier installs are UL 1741-SA (Phase 1-3 smart inverter).
ic_fast_track_kw: No size limit for NBT/NEM or Non-Export facilities: Rule 21 E.2.b.i says NBT, NEM-1, NEM-2 and all Non-Exporting Generating Facilities are evaluated under Fast Track (Initial Review Screens A-M, Supplemental Review Screens N-P). Other exporting facilities have a voltage-based size table in E.2.b.i that was NOT read (truncated fetch). Secondary source: about 3 MW on 12 kV or higher in PG&E.
ic_simplified_kw: 11 kVA - Screen J ('Is the Gross Rating of the Generating Facility 11 kVA or less?'). Screen K: NEM facility <=500 kW. Secondary source: ICA Screen M is not applied at <=30 kVA.
ic_application_fee: NBT/NEM <=1 MW: one-time fee set per IOU from historical costs - PG&E $145, SCE $94, SDG&E $132 (CPUC NEM/NBT page). These facilities are also exempt from Supplemental Review fees, study costs and distribution/network upgrade costs, and paired storage keeps the exemption if total nameplate is <=1 MW. Non-NEM, non-export and >1 MW requests: $800 Interconnection Request fee (Rule 21 Table E.1) plus study costs. Optional pre-application report: $300; enhanced reports $225, $800 or $1,025.
ic_study_trigger_kw: 1000 - above 1 MW the Rule 21 D.13 NBT/NEM exemptions end, and the customer pays study and upgrade costs and follows non-NEM timelines. At any size, failing Initial Review screens (e.g. Screen M ICA/15% of peak load) moves the project to Supplemental Review, then Independent Study or Distribution Group Study.
external_disconnect: Utility discretion - Rule 21 Sec. H.1.d / Hh.1.d 'Visible Disconnect Required'. Secondary source: PG&E does not require a separate AC disconnect where the service has a single-phase self-contained revenue meter. The local AHJ may still require one.
insurance_required: Unclear - no Rule 21 insurance requirement for NBT/NEM facilities was found in the portion of Rule 21 read (the tariff fetch was truncated before the insurance provisions).
ic_timeline_days: NBT/NEM <=1 MW: PTO normally within 30 business days after receipt of a complete request, a signed agreement and final electrical inspection (Rule 21 D.13.b). Pre-application report: 10 business days. Secondary source: NGOM install 40 business days; distribution upgrades 120 business days (D.20-09-035). Non-Export Energy Storage may elect the expedited process in Rule 21 Sec. N (D.14).
non_export_option: Yes - well defined. Rule 21 Screen I (G.1.i) non-export and limited-export options: reverse-power or minimum-power relays; certified Power Control Systems (PCS) with open-loop response time of 2 s or less can use Fast Track (Secondary: Energy Toolbase summary of the Res. E-5000-era changes). Other paths: Sec. M / Mm inadvertent export using UL 1741 SA-listed inverters; Sec. N expedited interconnection for Non-Export Energy Storage; Sec. O certified non-export AC/DC converters; Rule 21 Non-Export agreement. NEM/NBT expansions above the 10%/1 kW limit can go on a Non-Export agreement without losing legacy status. Limited Generation Profiles (Res. E-5230 workshops) are an emerging path.
storage_counts_toward_cap: No for the sized-to-load test, which uses renewable generator output only. Yes for the 1 MW threshold: Integrated or Directly Connected storage nameplate is added to aggregate facility nameplate (SCE Sched. NBT SC 1.b.iii.B). Large paired storage (>10 kW AC) is capped at 150% of the renewable generator's maximum output (D.19-01-030). D.20-06-017 suspended that cap from 2020-08-16; an Executive Director extension ran it to 2025-08-15. Whether the 150% cap is now enforced again is Unclear. Small paired storage (<=10 kW) has no relative size limit. SCE Sched. NBT SC 5.a.ii (Sheet 27, Advice 5228-E) says the waiver was extended by the Executive Director on 2023-09-05 and the 150% limit 'shall not apply until on and after August 16, 2025' - read literally the cap applies again from 2025-08-16; no later extension found, but not confirmed either. No limit on storage kWh.
standby_charge: None for NEM/NBT generation: NEM customers are exempt from standby charges (CPUC NEM page), and SCE Sched. NBT Rates 5 says no Standby or Customer Generation Departing Load charges apply to the NBT generating facility's capacity. Non-eligible generators on the same premises are not exempt.

rule_citation: N.C.G.S. 62-126.4 (H589, S.L. 2017-192); NCUC Docket E-100 Sub 180 Order Approving Revised Net Metering Tariffs (Mar 23 2023) + Order Granting Extension (May 17 2023) and Duke compliance tariffs filed Apr 3 2023 (DEC Leaf 72 Rider NM, Leaf 143 Rider NMB, Leaf 141 Rider RSC; DEP Riders NM-5, NMB-1, RSC-2); NC Interconnection Procedures (NCIP) eff. June 14 2019, Docket E-100 Sub 101 (text: https://www.duke-energy.com/_/media/pdfs/rates/ncinterconnections-dep.pdf?la=en)
applies_to: IOU only (Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress, Dominion Energy NC). EMCs and municipals are not rate-regulated by NCUC and are not required to offer net metering; they set their own rules (see utility file)
nem_successor: Legacy Rider NM closed to new residential applicants (tariff text July 1 2023; extended to 9/30/2023 by May 17 2023 order); legacy residential participants must transfer to Rider NMB or another rider by Jan 1 2027. Successors: Rider RSC (Residential Solar Choice; requires Schedule R-TOU-CPP; netting within each TOU period incl. separate CPP period; NEEC for net excess; NBC; grid access fee above 15 kW; minimum bill) and Rider NMB (Net Metering Bridge; same credit/NBC/minimum bill but on any rate; annual kW enrollment caps; closed to new participants Jan 1 2027; Bridge Rate Period up to 15 calendar years from submission date of the applicable interconnection application, then transfer to RSC). Non-residential Rider NM not closed by these tariffs. BATTERY RETROFIT: riders require written notice of any Nameplate Capacity change within 60 days; neither NMB nor RSC text says a battery addition restarts the 15-yr Bridge term or forces a move to RSC - Unclear (a new interconnection application for the battery could arguably be 'the applicable interconnection application'; not addressed). MID-TRANSITION: legacy-to-NMB migration Jan 2027
nem_cap_res_kw: 20 kW AC and not more than estimated maximum monthly demand of the residence (Riders NMB/RSC)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 1000 kW (legacy Rider NM, lesser of estimated max annual kW demand or 1,000 kW)
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap. Rider NMB annual enrollment capacity (kW AC, first-come first-served, reserved at interconnection application): DEC 2023 14,500 / 2024 31,900 / 2025 35,100 / 2026 38,700; DEP 2023 16,350 / 2024 35,900 / 2025 39,500 / 2026 43,500. Applicants after the annual cap must reapply next year or take RSC. Current subscription level not verified
nem_sizing_rule: Residential (NMB/RSC): nameplate <= lesser of estimated max monthly demand of residence or 20 kW AC. Non-residential legacy NM: <= lesser of estimated max annual kW demand or 1,000 kW
export_credit_value: Net Excess Energy Credit (NEEC): DEC 3.35 c/kWh, DEP 3.40 c/kWh (compliance tariffs eff. July 2023; later biennial updates not checked). Legacy Rider NM: 1:1 retail kWh (TOU customers netted by period)
credit_rollover: Successor riders: monthly net excess credited in dollars at NEEC; credits roll forward (no forfeiture per installer summary). Legacy Rider NM: kWh credits roll monthly, forfeited annually
annual_true_up: Legacy Rider NM only: unused credits forfeited June 1 (DEC) / May 31 (DEP) with no payment. Successor riders: no annual forfeiture (monthly NEEC crediting)
ic_standard: NCIP (June 14 2019) Attachment 4: IEEE 1547 + IEEE 1547.1 testing, UL 1741 certified equipment (edition not specified). IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741-SB implementation tracked by annual utility reports in Docket E-100 Sub 101B (Duke report Apr 1 2020; DENC Mar 15 2021); a dated mandatory 1547-2018 cutover was not found
ic_fast_track_kw: Certified UL inverter-based only. Line <5 kV: 100 kW (500 kW if on mainline and <=2.5 circuit miles from substation); 5-15 kV: 1 MW (2 MW); 15-35 kV: 2 MW; >=35 kV ineligible
ic_simplified_kw: 20 kW (Section 2 20 kW Inverter Process for certified inverter-based facilities)
ic_application_fee: $200 non-refundable (20 kW Inverter Process form, 2019 NCIP; 2015 NCIP was $100); Fast Track $750 (>20-100 kW), $1,000 (>100 kW-2 MW); Supplemental Review deposit $750 (>20-100 kW) and higher above; $500 pre-application report; $500 change of ownership; Study Process deposit + $1/kW AC capped at $100,000 aggregate
ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Fast Track limits (100 kW-2 MW depending on line voltage/location), non-inverter or uncertified equipment, lines >=35 kV, or failure of Fast Track/Supplemental Review screens -> Section 4 Study Process (System Impact + Facilities studies)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (NCIP 6.16: utility may require lockable, visible, accessible manual load-break disconnect; for certified inverter-based <=10 kW where not otherwise code-required, utility reimburses reasonable cost)
insurance_required: Residential <=250 kW: homeowner's policy with >= $100,000/occurrence liability; non-residential <=250 kW: CGL >= $300,000; non-residential >250 kW: CGL >= $1,000,000 (NCIP 6.15; self-insurance allowed if creditworthy)
ic_timeline_days: 20 kW process: utility has 15 business days to verify screens; Fast Track initial review within 15 business days of complete request; witness test within 10 business days of Certificate of Completion
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (NCIP defines Generating Facility to include storage and asks kWh; adding storage/DC equipment not a Material Modification if output profile unchanged, NCIP 1.5.2. NEM riders admit only storage charged solely from onsite renewables)
grid_charging_allowed: No - Riders NM, NMB and RSC (DEC and DEP) only admit 'an energy storage device configured to receive electrical charge solely from onsite renewable energy generation'. A grid-charged battery would have to sit outside net metering (non-NEM arrangement not verified)
non_export_option: Partial: NCIP Interconnection Request asks for an hourly max import/export profile (flows above it = Adverse Operating Effect), and a Standby Generating Facility with zero export gets expedited Section 4 study (NCIP 1.8.3.4). No dedicated non-export Fast Track screen found
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - 20 kW AC cap applies to 'Nameplate Capacity of Customer's installed generation system and equipment'; NBC/GAF billed per kW DC for solar or kW AC for non-solar; battery kW treatment not stated
standby_charge: Not a standby charge per se: NBC $0.28/kW-mo (DEC) / $0.62/kW-mo (DEP) on nameplate; RSC Grid Access Fee $2.05 (DEC) / $1.50 (DEP) per kW above 15 kW; monthly minimum bill (customer+distribution portion) $22 (DEC NMB, DEC RSC, DEP NMB) / $28 (DEP RSC). DEP Rider NM-5: standby not required for residential or general service <=100 kW
standby_threshold_kw: 15 kW (RSC grid access fee); 100 kW general service (DEP legacy NM standby waiver)

jurisdiction_body: Public Service Commission of South Carolina (PSCSC); Office of Regulatory Staff
rule_citation: S.C. Code 58-40-20 as amended by Act 62 of 2019 (SC Energy Freedom Act) - Solar Choice Metering; PSCSC Order 2021-390 (Duke, Docket 2020-264-E) and Order 2021-391 (DESC, Docket 2020-229-E); Order 2025-453 (DEC Rider NMT); SC Generator Interconnection Procedures eff. June 18 2021, Docket 2019-326-E, Order 2021-439 (https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/0d678dc4-2ccb-4938-8f9c-cf3982a3b781); DESC Solar Choice rider https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/36cec7b8-fe00-411a-87a1-320edcf87331; DEC Rider NMT https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/ec070b41-9f5f-4c6f-a11a-480e0b73b559
applies_to: IOU only (Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress, Dominion Energy South Carolina). Santee Cooper (state authority), electric cooperatives and munis are not bound by these tariffs and set their own net metering/interconnection rules (see utility file)
nem_successor: Act 62 Solar Choice Metering tariffs for applications on/after June 1 2021: Duke Rider RSC (requires Schedule R-STOU; netting within each TOU period, CPP exports netted against On-Peak; net excess per TOU period credited at avoided-cost-based rate; NBC per kW; minimum bill); DESC Solar Choice rider to Rate 5 (TOU kWh netting by period, kWh bank to November; minimum term 10 yrs). Legacy Duke Rider RNM (1:1): applications before 5/16/2019 through 12/31/2025; 5/16/2019-5/31/2021 through 5/31/2029. MID-TRANSITION: DEC Rider NMT (Order 2025-453, eff. 1/1/2026) takes legacy RNM/IRSC customers for up to 10 yrs (to 12/31/2035 for pre-5/16/2019 apps; 6/1/2029-5/31/2039 for later apps) with monthly netting and NEEC for excess, then Rider RSC. BATTERY RETROFIT: NMT/RSC dates are keyed to the 'original interconnection application date for the generation system' and customers must report Nameplate Capacity changes within 60 days; neither rider says a battery addition resets dates - Unclear, but the storage-charging restriction below would apply
nem_cap_res_kw: 20 kW AC (Act 62 customer-generator definition; Duke RSC/NMT and DESC Solar Choice riders)
nem_aggregate_cap: None stated in the Solar Choice riders read (legacy DESC 2015 rider had a 0.2% of SC retail peak cap; that rider is closed)
nem_sizing_rule: Customer-generator must be 'intended primarily to offset part or all of the customer-generator's own electrical energy requirements'; <=20 kW AC residential
export_credit_value: DEC Rider RSC: $0.0397/kWh net excess per TOU period (Leaf 136 eff. 1/1/2024); DEC Rider NMT: 4.19 c/kWh (eff. 1/1/2026). DESC Solar Choice: excess kWh offsets same-TOU-period usage in later months; unused bank paid at avoided cost (Rate PR-1 off-peak winter energy credit) each November
credit_rollover: Duke: monthly dollar credit at NEEC (no kWh bank). DESC: kWh bank rolls monthly within TOU period, cash-out at avoided cost in November
annual_true_up: DESC: November billing cycle, unused excess kWh paid at avoided cost and bank zeroed. Duke RSC/NMT: none (monthly crediting)
ic_standard: SC Generator Interconnection Procedures (June 18 2021) Attachment: IEEE 1547 + IEEE 1547.1 testing, UL certified inverters (edition not specified in text). No dated IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB mandate found
ic_fast_track_kw: Certified UL inverter-based only. Line <5 kV: 100 kW (500 kW on mainline <=2.5 circuit miles from substation); 5-25 kV: 1 MW (2 MW); >=25 kV not eligible
ic_simplified_kw: 20 kW (Section 2 20 kW Inverter Process; utility reserves circuit capacity per phase for <=20 kW projects)
ic_application_fee: Fast Track/20 kW: $100 (<=20 kW), $250 (>20-100 kW), $500 (>100 kW-2 MW); $50 transfer of ownership; Study Process deposits separate (Duke cluster appendix $10,000 study deposit)
ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Fast Track limits (100 kW-2 MW by voltage/location) or failure of Fast Track screens -> Section 4 serial Study Process, or Commission-authorized Cluster Study (utility appendix)
external_disconnect: Required for 20 kW Inverter Process per its Terms and Conditions (manual load-break disconnect immediately adjacent to utility meter unless utility agrees otherwise); utility discretion above; utility reimburses cost for certified inverter-based <=10 kW when not code-required
insurance_required: Residential <=250 kW: homeowner's policy >= $100,000/occurrence; non-residential <=250 kW: CGL >= $300,000; non-residential >250 kW higher (amount not read)
ic_timeline_days: 20 kW process: utility has 15 business days to complete screening; witness test within 10 business days or deemed waived
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (customer-generator definition includes energy storage charged solely from onsite renewables; SC GIP application collects storage data)
grid_charging_allowed: No - Act 62 customer-generator definition, repeated in Duke RSC/NMT and DESC Solar Choice riders, covers only 'an energy storage device configured to receive electrical charge solely from an onsite renewable energy resource'
non_export_option: Unclear - no defined non-export/limited-export screen found in SC GIP text searched
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - 20 kW AC cap applies to 'Nameplate Capacity of Customer's installed generation system and equipment'; NBC billed on kW DC for solar or kW AC for non-solar
standby_charge: No standby charge for Solar Choice residential. Duke: non-bypassable charge per nameplate kW (NMT: $0.45/kW for apps on/after 6/1/2021; RSC amount not read); NMT minimum customer & distribution charge $10; RSC minimum bill = Basic Facilities Charge plus rate-schedule minimum. DESC Solar Choice minimum bill $13.50/month

jurisdiction_body: Georgia Public Service Commission (Georgia Power); EMC and municipal governing bodies for their own systems
rule_citation: Georgia Cogeneration and Distributed Generation Act of 2001, O.C.G.A. 46-3-50 to 46-3-56; Georgia Power Schedule RNR-11 (eff. Jan 2023 bills; GPSC Dockets 4822 and 16573); Georgia Power Rules and Regulations Section G (Customer Generation) https://www.georgiapower.com/content/dam/georgia-power/pdfs/business-pdfs/tariffs/2023/Rules-Regs.pdf; GPC BTM Interconnection Summary (Residential) rev. 08.15.2025 https://www.georgiapower.com/content/dam/georgia-power/pdfs/company-pdfs/solar-pdfs/btm-distribution-interconnection-summary-residential.pdf
applies_to: All utilities for the statutory purchase obligation ('electric service provider' includes electric utilities, EMCs and municipal utilities); PSC sets rates/interconnection terms only for Georgia Power; EMCs and munis set price and interconnection rules through their own governing bodies (46-3-56(b),(d))
nem_successor: Georgia Power RNR-Monthly Netting (5,000-customer pilot) closed to new participants; non-transferable, 15-year term expiring no later than 12/31/2038, then automatic move to RNR-Instantaneous Netting. New customers: RNR-Instantaneous Netting (every kWh exported at any instant credited at Solar Avoided Energy Cost + 4 c/kWh adder)
nem_cap_res_kw: 10 kW AC (statute and RNR; capacity = aggregate inverter nameplate at service point)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 100 kW (statute); Georgia Power RNR allows commercial up to 250 kW AC (100-250 kW limited to 125% of prior-year metered peak demand)
nem_aggregate_cap: 0.2% of the utility's previous-year annual peak demand (O.C.G.A. 46-3-56(a); GPC RNR-Instantaneous first-come first-served to 0.2%); once subscribed, provider may purchase at a price set by PSC/governing body. Subscription level not verified
nem_sizing_rule: GPC: 100-250 kW commercial <=125% of preceding year's metered peak demand; no residential consumption-based rule in RNR-11
export_credit_value: GPC RNR-Instantaneous: Solar Avoided Energy Cost (updated annually under Renewable Cost Benefit framework, Docket 16573; value not read) + 4 c/kWh Renewable Generation Adder. RNR-Monthly (legacy): excess kWh offsets monthly consumption, remainder at Solar Avoided Energy Cost
credit_rollover: Monthly: credits summed monthly and applied to that month's bill (carryover of credits exceeding the bill not stated in tariff)
annual_true_up: None stated
ic_standard: Georgia Power: Southern Company DER Parallel Operation policy; inverters and AC-coupled battery gateways must be listed UL 1741 SB and IEEE 1547-2018 (BTM Summary 2025); >=250 kW needs local communications interface per IEEE 1547-2018 (Rules and Regs G.3). Statute requires NEC/NESC/IEEE/UL compliance only
ic_fast_track_kw: No statewide tiered fast-track; Georgia Power uses a single PowerClerk BTM process below 250 kW
ic_application_fee: Georgia Power: one-time $100 residential, $200 commercial/industrial; for <250 kW covers review, metering/programming and witness testing (Rules and Regs G.4)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 250 kW (Georgia Power: system impact study + witness testing mandatory at >=250 kW; smaller units only if deemed a risk)
external_disconnect: Required by Georgia Power (one-line must show generation AC disconnect(s) isolating the facility, visible load-break details per Construction Guidelines); no statewide rule
insurance_required: Statute bars providers from requiring additional liability insurance from a compliant customer generator (O.C.G.A. 46-3-56(e))
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (GPC: UL 1741 SB/IEEE 1547-2018 inverters; backup-capable systems need open-transition, mechanically interlocked transfer switch and DB 18-23 non-export form)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - RNR-11 credits any metered 'Excess Energy' delivered to the grid and says nothing about battery charging source; GPC summary describes batteries for 'self-consumption only' use; no rule found that bars or permits crediting of grid-charged exports
non_export_option: Yes - Georgia Power Energy Offset Only (EOO) agreement (no export, no compensation, utility may require export-prevention equipment; default if customer does not pick a program); DB 18-23 non-exporting generator form
storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes (Georgia Power): AC capacity is aggregate inverter nameplate at the service point; a battery system with maximum inverter capability >10 kW (even if derated) makes a residential customer ineligible for RNR
standby_charge: None found. RNR single-directional metering charge $5.97/mo (single-phase) or $12.66/mo (poly-phase) where used; bi-directional metering free

applies_to: IOU only (FPL, Duke Energy Florida, Tampa Electric, FPUC). Municipals and co-ops are exempt from 25-6.065 but s. 366.91(6) F.S. requires each muni and retail co-op to adopt its own standardized interconnection agreement and net metering program (governing body sets terms; annual report to FPSC) -- see utility file deltas
nem_successor: None. Full retail NEM survives; 2022 HB 741 (which would have phased NEM down) was vetoed. No open FPSC rulemaking to change 25-6.065 found as of 2026-09-24
nem_aggregate_cap: None in rule
nem_sizing_rule: Gross power rating (AC = DC x 0.85) must not exceed 90% of customer's distribution service rating; rule sets no consumption-based cap, but utility guidelines add one (e.g. FPL <115% of annual kWh)
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (monthly kWh carry-forward); annual cash-out at avoided cost
export_credit_value: Monthly excess credited as kWh against next bill at retail; year-end unused credits paid at average annual rate of utility's COG-1 as-available energy tariff (utility-specific, not a single statewide value)
credit_rollover: kWh credits roll monthly for up to 12 months; cash-out at avoided cost (COG-1) at end of calendar year and on account closure
annual_true_up: End of each calendar year (December bill): unused kWh credits paid at average annual COG-1 as-available energy rate
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (2003) + IEEE 1547.1 (2005) + UL 1741 (2005) per rule text -- rule not updated for IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB; utility agreements cite IEEE 1547/UL 1741 current editions generically
ic_fast_track_kw: 10 (Tier 1: no design review, no fees, no insurance); 100 (Tier 2: no further design review or extra equipment beyond disconnect)
ic_application_fee: Tier 1: none allowed; Tier 2 and Tier 3: utility-proposed, FPSC-approved cost-based fee (e.g. FPL $400 Tier 2, $1,000 Tier 3); Tier 3 may add an Interconnection Study Charge
ic_study_trigger_kw: 100 (Tier 3 >100 kW to 2 MW may require interconnection study)
external_disconnect: Waived for inverter-based Tier 1 (unless installed at utility expense); utility may require visible-break lockable manual disconnect for Tier 2/3
insurance_required: Tier 1: none (may be recommended); Tier 2: general liability up to $1M; Tier 3: up to $2M
ic_timeline_days: 10 business days completeness notice; agreement executed within 30 calendar days of complete application (90 days if Tier 3 study); inspection within 30 days of executed agreement
non_export_option: Not in rule. Stand-alone/grid-charged storage goes through the utility's Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (non-export -> no agreement needed at FPL if no utility equipment required)
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (rule and tiers are defined on renewable gross power rating; battery not addressed in rule)
standby_charge: Rule 25-6.065(8)(h): NEM customer continues to pay customer and demand charges; may at its discretion elect utility's standby/supplemental service rate. No mandatory standby charge on NEM customers
standby_threshold_kw: N/A (no mandatory standby charge on NEM customers; standby rate optional per 25-6.065(8)(h))

rule_citation: No statewide net metering or DG interconnection statute/rule. APSC-approved Alabama Power tariffs govern: Rate Rider RGB (Informal Docket U-4226, order 11/5/2021, eff. April 2022 billings); Rate PAE + Special Rules PAE (Docket 18005); APC DER Interconnection Process (July 2025) and DER Technical Interconnection Requirements Guidebook V3.2 (Feb 2026)
applies_to: No statewide rule. APSC regulates Alabama Power only among retail utilities with DG tariffs; TVA-served munis/co-ops in north AL follow TVA (see TN row / Huntsville Utilities delta); non-TVA co-ops (PowerSouth members) and munis set their own terms
nem_successor: No net metering at Alabama Power: exported energy bought at avoided cost under Rate PAE (<=100 kW; >100 kW Rate CPE contract); customer-generators must take Rate Rider RGB back-up service (capacity reservation charge)
nem_cap_res_kw: N/A (no NEM). Rate PAE sellback available to facilities <=100 kW nameplate
nem_cap_nonres_kw: N/A (no NEM). Rate PAE <=100 kW; larger via Rate CPE
nem_aggregate_cap: None (no NEM program)
nem_sizing_rule: None (no NEM)
export_credit_value: Alabama Power Rate PAE (44th rev., eff. April 2023 billings, as posted): TOD option Jun-Sep 7.44c/kWh weekdays 10am-9pm CT, 5.23c other; Oct-May 4.86c weekdays 7am-9pm, 4.41c other. Time Advantage option 4.40-7.69c/kWh; FD-D option 4.41-6.73c/kWh. Monthly base charge $0.97 (1-ph) / $1.91 (3-ph)
credit_rollover: PAE credits exceeding charges carried forward on account; check issued on customer request or termination
annual_true_up: None (no NEM)
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018; UL 1741-SA or -SB listed inverters for Tier I/II, UL 1741-SB for Tier III (APC DER TIR Guidebook V3.2, Feb 2026)
ic_fast_track_kw: 25 (Tier I, no study fee, 1-2 week review)
ic_application_fee: Tier I <=25 kW: $0; Tier II >25-100 kW: $500; Tier III >100 kW: $1,000 screening fee (+ $300 optional pre-application; further studies ~$10k-$50k)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 100 (Tier III screening; detailed distribution/transmission study if screen fails)
external_disconnect: Required: manually operable, visible-break, lockable, 24/7-accessible AC disconnect isolating entire DER (Guidebook sec. 6.1)
insurance_required: <=25 kW: recommended only; >25 kW: general liability >= $1M per incident naming APC as insured (Special Rules PAE rule 13)
ic_timeline_days: No rule timeline; APC published targets: Tier I 1-2 wks, Tier II 2-4 wks, Tier III 4-12 wks (studies up to 26 wks). Design approval valid 365 days
non_export_option: Yes: Guidebook defines Non-Export Generation (NEG) / Limited-Export Generation; Power Control Systems (UL 1741 CRD PCS or UL 3141) accepted for software export limits; >100 kW export limit set by impact study with backup export-limit relay. NEG still requires interconnection application and RGB applies
storage_counts_toward_cap: Tiers set by total aggregate nameplate of DER energy conversion devices (batteries/inverters listed); whether battery inverter kW is added to PV kW for tiering and RGB nameplate billing: Unclear
standby_charge: Rate Rider RGB (required for any customer with parallel non-emergency on-site generation): Capacity Reservation Charge $5.41/kW-month (secondary) or $4.87/kW-month (primary) on generator nameplate (customer may request calculated actual capacity need); alternative for qualifying residential customers: Rate RTA with 71c/kWh energy charge Jun-Sep weekdays 3-5pm in lieu of CRC. PURPA challenge: FERC declined enforcement 2021; M.D. Ala. granted summary judgment for APSC/Alabama Power 2026-03-25; appeal status not verified
standby_threshold_kw: No size exemption: RGB applies to any parallel non-emergency generation (for customers on rates outside the listed schedules, generation must be <= lesser of 6% of max demand or 25 kW)

jurisdiction_body: Tennessee Valley Authority (federal; sets terms for its local power companies via wholesale power contracts). Tennessee Public Utility Commission has no jurisdiction over TVA LPCs
rule_citation: No Tennessee net metering or DG interconnection statute/rule. TVA Dispersed Power Production (DPP) Guidelines + Dispersed Power Price Schedule CSPP (PURPA avoided cost); TVA Green Connect program; each LPC interconnection agreement/policy
applies_to: TVA-served LPCs (munis and co-ops = essentially all of TN). Each LPC sets its own interconnection agreement, fees, insurance and disconnect rules; TVA sets the export purchase terms (DPP). Kingsport Power (AEP, TPUC-regulated) not covered here
nem_successor: Net metering not available in TVA service area (TVA Green Connect FAQ). Excess or all generation may be sold to TVA under DPP at avoided cost (5-year PPA with TVA; requires executed LPC interconnection agreement). TVA Green Power Providers (retail-plus premium) closed to new participants
nem_cap_res_kw: N/A (no NEM). DPP accepts renewable QFs up to 80 MW
nem_aggregate_cap: None for DPP
nem_sizing_rule: None (no NEM)
export_credit_value: TVA DPP Schedule CSPP eff. 2025-12-01: Part A (meters <500 kW or not time-differentiated) 3.766c/kWh flat; Part B (>500 kW interval-metered): Super Peak 4.261, On Peak 4.212, Off Peak 3.736, Super Off Peak 3.538 c/kWh. Revised monthly-to-annually by TVA
credit_rollover: None: DPP pays monthly via ACH for metered energy delivered to TVA (separately metered from LPC retail service)
annual_true_up: None
ic_standard: Set by each LPC (TVA requires anti-islanding trip <10 cycles in DPP PPA)
ic_fast_track_kw: None at TVA level (tiers, if any, set by each LPC)
ic_simplified_kw: None at TVA level (tiers, if any, set by each LPC)
ic_application_fee: Set by each LPC (varies)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 250 (TVA transmission screening for DPP facilities >250 kW; TVA transmission study if screen fails or >5 MVA)
external_disconnect: Set by each LPC
insurance_required: TVA requires none; many LPCs do (per TVA Green Connect FAQ)
ic_timeline_days: No TVA-level timeline; set by each LPC (e.g. MLGW technical review ~4-5 weeks; NES application due >=60 days before operation)
non_export_option: Yes in practice: behind-the-meter self-consumption without DPP enrollment still needs LPC interconnection agreement; non-export path rules set per LPC
storage_counts_toward_cap: N/A (no NEM cap)
standby_charge: None at TVA level; LPC-specific (TVA wholesale rate structure lets LPCs add grid-access/fixed charges)
standby_threshold_kw: N/A at TVA level (LPC-specific, e.g. MLGW availability charge on all self-generators)
